Product inputs (SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, feature specifications, task prompts) are not instruction layers and never silently override CLAUDE.md, the technology stack or path rules; such a request goes through Decision Control.
Reopening any Decided item (settled by product sources, CLAUDE.md, the technology stack, rules, accepted decision records or established project structure) requires approval.

It is ambiguous whether an explicit approval in the original request of a headless run allows a Reserved change, given 'an explicit user instruction counts as approval' and 'in a headless run never make a Reserved decision' (reported ambiguity).
.NET 10 is used on its latest stable servicing release (reported as more specific than .NET 10 LTS and C# 14).
No mapping framework other than Mapster without approval, and mapping-library concerns stay out of Domain.

reviewer_text: The dependency guard blocks npm commands that touch the force / legacy-peer-deps configuration keys or environment assignments regardless of intent, including read-only 'npm config get' and 'npm config set force false'.
The dependency guard's documented command parser is minimal (no npx npm, no encoded PowerShell commands), so enforcement is narrower than the npm bypass rule.

After any successful or failed shell command (not only dependency or reference commands), the hook checks manifests that are new, changed or removed relative to a persisted snapshot and adds owner routing.
The edit hook only enforces when the event carries a string file_path inside a resolvable checkout; other edit events finish silently.
After a direct edit of a .csproj, Directory.Packages.props or package.json, the hook runs the manifest check and returns violations as a blocking post-tool reason.
Hook change detection uses SHA-256 content identity but switches to size and modification time for files above 1 MiB.
Hook state is persisted in an override directory, the Git directory or a temp folder, and failure to persist it is swallowed.
The Stop co-change hook is skipped for recursive stops (stop_hook_active) and for unresolvable or non-Git environments.
Repository-root resolution scopes checks through the common Git directory and template offset; nested unrelated repositories inside the template resolve to the template root.
A skill folder may contain only SKILL.md and flat Markdown references (no scripts, assets or nested reference folders).
Project-reference checks classify projects only by file-name suffix; projects with other names are not classified.
Ordinary feature development must not introduce NgModules unless an integration or legacy dependency genuinely requires them (reported as a prohibition stronger than the standalone default).
Direct IConfiguration access is confined to composition and registration code (reported as a restriction stronger than discouraging scattered lookups).
Catch an exception only when the current layer can recover, translate it, perform a defined fallback, add context while preserving the original exception, or perform required cleanup.
By default, expected outcomes such as not-found, validation failures or rejected business operations are not logged as application errors.
Prefer one observable scenario per test; a multi-step test fits when the sequence itself is the behavior.
The default test-name pattern is MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior unless the project already has an established convention.
Direct Polly may be used only when the Microsoft resilience packages cannot express a concrete requirement, and the reason must be documented (reported as a restriction stronger than a default).
Use computed for derived state and avoid unnecessary effect() when computed, template binding or explicit event handling expresses the dependency more clearly.
If a project adopts a Result pattern, it must use typed errors rather than arbitrary strings passed through every layer (reported as a requirement).
Test authorization behavior of important protected operations: unauthenticated 401, unauthorized 403, permitted success, resource ownership rules and intended anonymous access.
Adding caching solely for performance requires a measurement first (reported as stronger than 'measured or reasoned need').
An optional local formatter must not become a mandatory CI gate unless the project adopts that policy.
Ordinary application services receive typed options; direct IConfiguration access belongs to the composition root, configuration-provider setup and infrastructure registration.
When a singleton or hosted service needs scoped work, create a scope per operation and resolve a scoped orchestration service, not Infrastructure internals.
The final development report must include noteworthy Delegated choices and, for each change-specific obligation that did not apply, the reason.
ASP.NET Core Dockerfiles use a multi-stage build.

Docker changes are verified by building the image and checking startup, ports and configuration, non-root behavior when relevant, health-probe integration, accidental secrets/files, and meaningful application tests.
Arrange/Act/Assert is the default test structure; comments are optional when the phases are obvious.
Keep slow or unreliable external-system tests separate from ordinary fast test runs.
Keep entity configuration separate with IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.
Paged queries always use deterministic ordering.
Observe retries, timeouts and circuit behavior when they materially affect operations.
Use a DelegatingHandler only for genuine HTTP pipeline concerns (authorization header acquisition, correlation propagation, request signing), never for business decisions.
When an application uses Serilog's static/bootstrap Log.Logger it flushes it on shutdown; purely host-managed logging follows the provider lifetime instead.
Use the official Elastic.Serilog.Sinks package instead of the deprecated Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch.
Choose log levels by operational meaning (Trace/Debug, Information, Warning, Error, Critical) and avoid logging every internal method call.
Before using a language feature confirm the configured language version supports it; do not change LangVersion or the target framework to use newer syntax.

Make each supporting type's responsibility clear from its name or directory (role suffixes), avoid ambiguous names such as TaskWorkflow, and add responsibility subdirectories only when a flat directory becomes hard to navigate.
global.json pins the repository to the intended .NET SDK line: the current stable SDK for the target release (no RC/preview unless requested) with patch/feature-band servicing through rollForward.
Remove the shared properties (target framework, nullable, implicit usings) that dotnet new duplicates into each project file; the target framework comes from Directory.Build.props.
Use OWASP Top 10:2025 as an awareness taxonomy when it fits; do not force an inaccurate category mapping.
For a new local Development API configure the launch profile to open Swagger when that helps, and keep application URLs and launch profile scheme/port in agreement.

Before completion remove unused or redundant using directives from every created or modified C# file (including those covered by implicit/global usings unless needed for clarity or disambiguation), verified on the changed files, without repository-wide cleanup.

New instruction content is placed by kind: planning-time governance and decisions in the compact CLAUDE.md or technology stack; area constraints in a flat path rule whose paths cover the needed scope; procedures, stop conditions and output formats in workflow skills; technique in knowledge skills or their references; mechanical checks in scripts or hooks plus a concise rule.
After placing new instruction content, MAP.md is updated and check-instructions is run.
If an omitted product detail must be decided to implement the requested behavior and materially affects observable behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Product behavior not defined by the product sources is a Reserved decision.
At Stop, the co-change hook raises reminders from broad path heuristics (model without seeder change, migration files, production without test changes).
The Stop reminder blocks finishing until Claude addresses each item or states why it does not apply.
The reminder state fingerprint covers at most 200 changed files.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics (not 200 for every outcome, not 201 merely because a row was inserted, not 202 for synchronously completed work); a 204 response has no body.
Keep status-code behavior consistent across similar endpoints.
A 204 response has no body.
Keep status-code behavior consistent across similar endpoints.

Dependencies point inward: Domain depends on no application project, Application on Domain, Infrastructure on Application and Domain, Api on Application and Infrastructure only for composition; never Domain -> Application/Infrastructure or Application -> Infrastructure.
Reconsider the abstraction instead of adding an outward project reference.
Program.cs is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.
Controllers do not consume Infrastructure implementation types directly.
Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked.
Avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work.
Do not reorganize existing files.
Do not convert constructors mechanically.
Keep implementation details non-public unless part of the public API; use sealed to communicate deliberate non-inheritance, not as a speculative optimization.

Use records when value semantics and immutability are desirable and classes when identity, mutable lifecycle, inheritance or framework behavior fit; do not turn every DTO or Domain type into a record.
Use var when the type is obvious or unimportant; use an explicit type when it improves clarity.
Use standard .NET naming (PascalCase/camelCase, meaningful names); private-field naming follows the repository convention.

Use npm for the Angular workspace unless another package manager is deliberately adopted; keep the lockfile consistent when packages change; build and test tooling goes into devDependencies unless there is a reason.
Maintain and commit package.json and package-lock.json.
Unexpected failures propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling; avoid broad try/catch blocks that only log and rethrow.
Catch an exception only to recover, translate, apply a defined fallback, add context while preserving the exception, or clean up.
Log an unexpected exception once at the boundary that handles it, not repeatedly across repository, Application, Controller and the global handler.
By default, expected outcomes (not-found, validation failures, rejected business operations) are not logged as application errors.

Compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, ArrayPool/MemoryPool, manual object pooling, custom serialization optimizations, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance are introduced only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.
Verify that an optimization materially improves the relevant workload.
Automatic development seeding runs only in the Development environment; never seed Production automatically.
Tests never use the development seeder.
Use descriptive test names communicating the scenario or condition and the expected behavior.
The default test-name pattern is MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior unless an established convention exists.
The instruction-system checker requires the required files (CLAUDE.md, technology stack, MAP.md, settings.json, code-reviewer agent, SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md) to exist.
CLAUDE.md imports only docs/technology-stack.md and no other instruction file contains an import.
Every instruction file starts with a one-line ownership header (Owns / Scope / Loads) whose Loads value matches its kind.
No instruction file contains Level:/Kind: classification lines.
.claude/rules stays flat (Markdown only) and every rule declares a non-empty paths list.
A skill folder holds SKILL.md plus optional Markdown references only.
The required workflow and knowledge skills exist and no competing serilog/resilience skills exist.
Skill frontmatter name equals the folder, descriptions are at most 1024 characters, knowledge descriptions start with 'Use when', and template-maintenance is user-only.
The code-reviewer agent stays a thin wrapper.
Private references are used only by their owning skill.
File, section and skill references in instruction files resolve.
MAP.md lists every instruction, hook and script file.
MAP.md is never imported.
An always-loaded estimate above about 6000 tokens is warned.
The checker requires a named inventory of instruction files to exist.
The checker requires the named workflow and knowledge skills to exist and forbids standalone serilog/resilience skills.
The checker defines a 6000-token warning threshold for the always-loaded budget.
CLAUDE.md may import only docs/technology-stack.md and no other instruction file may import.
Every instruction file needs the exact ownership header with the Loads value matching its kind.
Level:/Kind: classification lines are forbidden.
Rules stay flat Markdown files with a non-empty paths list.
Skill frontmatter name must equal the folder name, descriptions at most 1024 characters, knowledge descriptions start with a trigger prefix, and template-maintenance is user-only.

A skill's private references cannot be cited by another skill (MAP.md exempt) and must exist.
Backticked Markdown/repository references in instruction files must resolve, with docs/decisions exempt.
MAP.md must list every instruction, hook and script file.
Every settings.json hook must be registered in exact Node exec form with the script path anchored at CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
The PreToolUse guard must fail closed (onFailure block) and advisory hooks must not.
Hooks are registered in exec form (node plus the script path anchored at CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, no shell).
The dependency guard is registered for PostToolUseFailure.
The PreToolUse guard fails closed (onFailure block) while advisory hooks fail open.
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly and Polly.Extensions.Http are hard-denied by the manifest check, even with an explicit approval.
Other approval-gated packages (MediatR, Polly, Polly.Core, FluentValidation.AspNetCore, Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch) produce advisory notes only.

The deprecated Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch sink is not used without a concrete requirement (the manifest check flags it).

peerDependencies are not checked by the manifest checker.

A missing package-lock.json is only a note.
After a dependency change, run node .claude/scripts/check-manifests.mjs from the repository root.
Restore and build the affected projects.
Inspect vulnerability information for the changed dependency set.
Remove dependencies that are no longer used when that is part of the current change.
Report the package, selected version, license, checks performed and approval status.
After a dependency change run the manifest check.
After a dependency change restore and build the affected projects.
After a dependency change inspect vulnerability information for the changed dependency set.
Use provider-based HttpClient configuration when configuration is required.
Class-based interceptors need a reason.
When the project uses Angular Material use it consistently; do not add it automatically to a project that has not chosen it; do not wrap every Material component without a concrete reason.
When OpenAPI client generation is adopted keep generated code separate from handwritten logic and regenerate it when the contract changes.
Test frontend behavior at the appropriate level, keep E2E to a few important workflows unless more is required, and do not duplicate the same behavior at every level.
Generate separate or grouped OpenAPI descriptions for supported versions when clients need them, matching runtime routing and Controller metadata.
When versions coexist, test version routing, version-specific shapes, deprecated-version operation, unsupported-version behavior and shared-behavior consistency, without duplicating identical tests.
A Decision Request must present a title, Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked work and Proceeding-with work.

An approved Reserved decision (including an explicit instruction in the original request) is recorded before its Reserved part is implemented.

The planning-time owner is updated (CLAUDE.md Architecture Defaults or docs/technology-stack.md).
New path-rule constraints are edited into the owning rule.
Rejected or deferred decisions worth keeping are recorded with that status.
Follow the established validation invocation pattern rather than adding a second competing mechanism.
Do not add a deprecated automatic-validation integration package to connect FluentValidation.
Typed exceptions for selected cases are a consistent project-level decision, not a per-feature habit.
Prefer policy-based authorization when authorization logic is more than a trivial role check.
Choose the authentication scheme from the actual application (Bearer/OIDC for SPA to API, cookies for server-rendered apps, Identity for local accounts, external OIDC/OAuth for delegated identity).
Do not issue custom JWTs when an existing identity provider already owns token issuance.
Use stable constants for policy names repeated across the application.
Prefer a policy over scattered compound role strings when several roles or claims represent one capability.
Application never depends on HttpContext, ClaimsPrincipal or IHttpContextAccessor; repeated caller-identity needs use a small Application abstraction with an outer adapter.
Do not create ICurrentUser when passing an explicit user identifier is simpler.
Reproduce and diagnose the actual failure before editing.
Read the complete output, group errors by root cause and fix the highest-leverage root cause first.
For failing tests decide whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentionally changed contract is at fault.
For cross-stack failures determine the authoritative contract.
Update obsolete APIs from verified documentation; never fabricate replacement APIs.
Keep repair iterations small and bounded: rerun the narrowest failing verification after each meaningful fix and expand only after the focused failure is resolved.
Start with the narrowest command that reliably reproduces the problem.
Do not run unrelated build systems.
Stop and reassess when progress stalls.
Do not repeat variants of a failed guess.
Do not change the repository's declared SDK, Node, framework or language version because the local machine differs; report an unavailable toolchain instead of editing source.

Use bounded iteration and stop and reassess under concrete conditions (same root failure survives, new unrelated failures, incompatible toolchain, missing infrastructure, unresolvable packages, undeterminable behavior); do not repeat failed guesses.
When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine input is required.
Never claim a problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains.
Never leave the repository knowingly worse; unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.
Report an unavailable toolchain instead of editing source or changing declared SDK, Node, framework or language versions.
Do not weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests or compiler, TypeScript, lint or analyzer failures to make verification pass.
No strong-to-weak assertion swaps, any-casts, disabled strict mode or suppressed template diagnostics.
Update a test only for an actually requested contract change.

A build fix must not bypass architecture to compile (Application to Infrastructure references, DbContext in Application, business logic in Controllers, Angular-only authorization, HTTP calls scattered into components).
Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing.
Build and test the frontend through the scripts package.json actually defines; never invent script names or assume a test runner.
In CI install with npm ci and add test/lint commands only when the project defines them.
The build-fix report states the initial failure, root cause, changes made and remaining issues.
The build-fix report states backend build, frontend build and tests as PASS, NOT RUN or NOT APPLICABLE.
Decide explicitly whether a cache failure falls back to the source, fails the request or returns stale data.
Test cache behavior when it affects observable correctness (invalidation, isolation, miss fallback, outage policy); do not unit-test framework cache internals.
Avoid caching EF tracked entities across Unit of Work boundaries.
CI pipelines reproduce the repository's supported build and test commands.
Inspect the repository before writing a pipeline and do not assume a database, Redis, Docker or frontend tooling.
Add pipeline stages for the actual project.
Do not hardcode one database provider into a generic pipeline.
Do not make an unadopted formatter a mandatory CI gate.
Do not depend on developer-machine state.
Keep pipeline failures visible.
Prefer promoting the same tested artifact or image through environments instead of recompiling per environment.
Prefer workload/federated identity over long-lived deployment credentials when the platform supports it.
Use environment protection or approval appropriate to the hosting platform for deployment.
Before considering a pipeline complete, verify clean-environment restore, builds, configured tests, no developer-machine dependence, no secret exposure and expected artifacts.

Review prioritizes correctness, security/authorization, data integrity/persistence, architectural boundaries, concurrency/integration, missing meaningful tests, maintainability, then credible evidence-backed performance.
Style preferences are not elevated above behavioral defects.
Code is not reported as a violation merely for differing from an unadopted pattern.
Before judging, the review reads the changed code with enough surrounding code (callers, contracts, dependencies); no review of isolated lines.
The review identifies the intended behavior and the tests protecting it.
The review reads the rules whose paths match the changed files.
No hypothetical review findings without a plausible execution path.
No findings to populate categories; when no meaningful findings exist say so and state important areas that could not be verified.
Tool output is evidence rather than authority.
No filler praise.
Report findings ordered by severity, each with severity, file/location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix, using the Critical/High/Medium/Low scale.
Do not add filler praise to balance criticism.
Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Framework defaults the project has not intentionally overridden are not settings.
Record an approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value under a stable name with its value and purpose.

When an approved value is added, changed or removed, identify and update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored frontend/backend surface; one changed literal does not establish synchronization.

Search for stale references to the old value and setting name (validators and DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, database mapping, frontend validation and UI hints, tests and test data, documentation, mirrored configuration).
Update only affected behavior.
After a settings change build, test and run verify.
Register Application services, repositories and external adapters at architectural boundaries interface-to-implementation; concrete registration only for implementation-only helpers.
Prefer explicit registration in small and medium applications; add scanning, keyed services, factories or decorators only for an actual composition problem.
For a new application or substantial feature read SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md before planning or implementing.
Read every path rule matching the areas to be created or changed (explicitly for new files and greenfield work) and load the relevant knowledge skills.
Inspect the relevant existing code before a non-trivial change.
Read the owning rules before a non-trivial change; rules that have not loaded yet are read explicitly.

Whenever a Domain or persistence change affects seeded entities, update DbSeeder in the same change so recreating the Development database yields valid representative data; existing rows are not patched.
Review DbSeeder together with migrations that change seeded entities.
Copy only existing repository-level build files required by restore and copy project files explicitly; avoid wildcard tricks that flatten a multi-project structure.
Copy project and build dependency files before the full source tree for restore caching, update that section when the structure changes, and never trade restore correctness for caching.
Do not assume curl, wget or shell utilities in the runtime image; verify an in-container health command's executable exists or add a probe mechanism.
Exclude non-build files from the Docker build context, but never exclude tests the image build runs or files required by restore/build.
Use Alpine, chiseled, trimmed or Native AOT images only when justified and verify compatibility (globalization, native dependencies, reflection, diagnostics).
Use tracking intentionally (tracking for entities modified in the current Unit of Work, AsNoTracking for read-only entity queries, not mechanically on DTO projections).
Avoid lazy loading by default because it hides database access and causes N+1 queries.
Do not casually mix bulk ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete operations with tracked entities for the same rows; understand their transaction implications.
Do not attempt distributed transactions with EF transaction APIs.
Compiled queries pay off only on a measured hot path where profiling shows material compilation overhead.
Do not hide business behavior in persistence interceptors.
Use representative root/anchor entities to detect existing seed data.
Complex seed datasets should be described explicitly by the task requirements rather than invented.
Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.
Do not automatically stash, reset or discard work to make a merge or rebase proceed.
Never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work.

Before a repository-changing Git operation inspect the repository state (git status, git diff, git diff --cached), use the minimum operation required and do not silently clean up unrelated working-tree changes.
Do not rename existing user branches to satisfy a naming convention.
Do not push unrelated local commits accidentally.
Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the intended logical change; do not stage unrelated files merely because they are modified.
Implementation and its tests belong in the same logical commit; no artificial tiny commits.
Do not combine unrelated fixes into one commit.
Follow the repository's branch-naming convention, otherwise use prefixes such as feature/, fix/, refactor/, test/, docs/, chore/ with meaningful names.
Prefer one logical change per commit, with implementation and its tests together and no artificial tiny commits.
Follow the repository commit-message convention, otherwise Conventional Commits.
Before removing a worktree verify required changes are committed or preserved; never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work.
Parallel implementation work uses separate branches or worktrees and keeps unrelated changes out of the current branch.
One branch is not checked out in multiple normal worktrees.
Each worktree stays focused on its branch's concern.
Ensure relevant verification has completed before pushing.
Do not automatically stash, reset or discard work to make a merge or rebase proceed.
Run verify before preparing a pull request.
Treat main, master and other protected or shared branches as non-rewritable.
Destructive Git operations may be performed when explicitly requested or clearly required by an approved workflow.
main, master and other protected or shared branches are treated as non-rewritable.
A shared branch is never force-pushed unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting and the consequences are understood.
Check an external dependency only when it matters to readiness and avoid readiness cascades; prefer a lightweight check of the needed capability.
Keep probe responses small and protect detailed diagnostics with network or authorization controls.
Avoid Error-level logs for every normal failed probe.
Include a Location header identifying a created resource when a stable resource URI exists.
For 202 responses, when practical return an operation identifier or a Location to observe progress.
Choose consistently whether a repeated DELETE of an absent resource returns 204 or 404, and do not mix them between equivalent resources.
Use 304 only for conditional requests whose cached representation is still valid, never as a generic business 'nothing changed' response.
400 is for an invalid HTTP request (malformed, binding failure, uninterpretable), not for authentication failure.
Use 406 when no acceptable response representation can be produced and 415 when the request media type is unsupported; do not confuse them.
Use 422 for structurally valid requests with invalid semantic/business content; follow an established 400-for-both convention, otherwise 400 for contract errors and 422 for semantic errors.
Use 428 when a contract-required precondition such as If-Match is absent; other mandatory preconditions only when the contract defines them.
A rate-limited request returns 429 with Retry-After when the retry time is known; validation failures are not represented as rate limiting.
502 and 504 are only for an API acting as an intermediary (invalid upstream response, upstream timeout); do not map every dependency failure or TaskCanceledException to them.
503 for temporary inability, with Retry-After when a meaningful retry time is known.
With an idempotency key, reuse of the same key with a materially different payload is a reasonable 409, and idempotency is not claimed merely because duplicates are unlikely.
When HTTP optimistic concurrency is part of the contract prefer standard conditional request semantics over custom status codes.
Apply per-request values such as dynamic access tokens to the specific request or through a handler; do not mutate shared DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently.
Prefer System.Net.Http.Json / System.Text.Json where sufficient and use explicit serialization options when the external contract differs.
Do not reuse internal Domain entities as remote API contracts merely to avoid mapping.
Do not retry validation errors, authentication/authorization failures, permanent 404 outcomes or deterministic business rejections.
Do not invent a client-side Idempotency-Key unless the remote service supports that contract.
Use hedging only for operations safe to execute multiple times, never for state-changing operations by default.

Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline by default; prefer provider execution strategies; an HTTP retry policy is not automatically appropriate for databases.
Retrying publication can duplicate delivery; use idempotent consumers, broker deduplication or outbox when required.
Prefer runtime trace identifiers for correlation; add an explicit correlation identifier only when a requirement needs one; propagate tracing context across outbound calls.
Validate or normalize a correlation identifier accepted from an external client before propagating it.
Do not use logs as an audit database unless a dedicated audit design has been adopted.

Repository-level Directory.Build.props holds genuinely shared .NET build settings (target framework, nullable, implicit usings, analysis/compiler settings); project-specific settings stay in their owning projects.
Directory.Packages.props holds Central Package Management.
Properties duplicated into project files by dotnet new are removed.
Ignore generated and local artifacts (bin, obj, .vs, node_modules, dist, .angular, TestResults, coverage, local secret/config overrides).
Do not ignore files intentionally part of the Development configuration contract, such as a non-secret appsettings.Development.json.

The security scan report contains Scope, a Limitations statement (static analysis only), a severity Summary table, Findings and Layer Results for the seven layers using PASS / FINDINGS / NOT APPLICABLE / NOT CHECKED.
The security scan uses the fixed severity scale Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info with defined meanings.
Investigation prompts are not automatic vulnerability declarations.
Report concrete risks and distinguish confirmed findings from items needing verification.
Rate severity by exploitability, reachability, exposure and impact rather than mechanically by pattern, CVSS or OWASP category.
Avoid known false positives.
Do not claim a static scan proves design security.
Do not invent exploitability.
Do not upgrade packages during a scan unless asked.
The security scan works without any specific MCP server, agent, analyzer, commercial scanner or external tool; tooling is evidence, never the sole authority.
A scanner-reported issue is reported only after inspecting the actual code and its reachability.
Security findings are reported in a fixed shape: severity tag, file:line location and title, OWASP category when applicable, Evidence, Impact (why it is a risk) and Remediation.
Uncertain findings use the NEEDS VERIFICATION form stating what the effective behavior depends on.
Every confirmed finding includes severity, file and location, title, evidence, why it is a risk, likely impact, smallest remediation and OWASP category when applicable.
Report per-layer results with PASS, FINDINGS, NOT APPLICABLE or NOT CHECKED, and never mark an uninspected layer as passed.
When command execution is genuinely needed prefer APIs that separate executable and arguments and validate or constrain external input.
Normalize user-influenced paths and verify they remain within the intended storage boundary.
Do not deserialize untrusted payloads into arbitrary runtime types.

Swagger UI through Swashbuckle.AspNetCore is the default interactive API documentation and manual-testing surface in Development (/swagger), rather than a standalone raw OpenAPI endpoint or built-in AddOpenApi()/MapOpenApi().
No second competing API documentation stack without a concrete need.
Avoid unstable anonymous response shapes and anonymous objects as long-lived contracts; use explicit request/response contracts.
When API behavior changes open the Development Swagger UI to confirm it loads and exercise representative endpoints when meaningful.
Instruction maintenance runs only when the user invokes it; Claude must not start it automatically.
Instruction-ownership invariants: one authoritative owner per policy with pointers elsewhere, each policy kept at its trigger, knowledge skills and private references hold technique only.
Product inputs stay inputs and do not carry instructions.
After maintenance update MAP.md and run the structure checker, fixing every failure.
For hook or script changes run the changed script with sample input and confirm both the pass and failure paths.
After hook or script changes run the changed script with sample input and confirm both the pass and the failure paths.
The maintenance report lists the files changed, owners added or moved and the checker result.

Verification starts with the final changed-file set and diff: the change matches the requested scope without unrelated refactoring, no generated or build artifacts or secrets were added, and temporary probes are removed only after preservation.

After all fixes the final diff is reviewed for unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, TODO/FIXME markers, stale temporary tests or scripts, architecture drift, unapproved product drift and stale surfaces after a settings change.
Do not use --no-restore unless restore is known to be complete.
For small solutions run the complete test suite; for large solutions run affected test projects first, then broader suites as required.
Build the affected projects; a solution that does not build is not complete (never report successful scaffolding for it).
Run the relevant tests.
All files use UTF-8, space indentation, a final newline and trimmed trailing whitespace, except that Markdown keeps trailing whitespace.
Indent 2 spaces for JSON/YAML, project/XML and TS/JS/HTML/SCSS/CSS files (single quotes for TS/JS) and 4 spaces for C#.
Interfaces must begin with I (warning severity).
Fields, properties, methods and events are not qualified with this.
Async methods are expected to end with Async, but detection only covers async-modified methods and no framework/interface contract exemption is encoded.
var is suggested when the type is apparent; explicit types elsewhere are allowed.
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; on an apparent conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected rather than choosing one.
Resolve a conflict between SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md before changing implementation.

Do not silently invent a value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior when no product source defines it: propose it with its reason, ask for approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and synchronize it through custom-settings.
Undefined tunable values are a Reserved decision.
Do not introduce CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization unless explicitly approved.
The manifest check notes a MediatR reference as requiring an approved decision.
NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind and additional form, component or state-management libraries are not added by default; an extra library is added only for a concrete need.
The manifest check notes these packages.
Changing an accepted project or architecture decision is Reserved (explicit approval unless already required by the specification or established structure).
A new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS/MediatR/Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices) is Reserved.
A new production project, layer or assembly or an additional DbContext/persistence boundary is Reserved.
Changed persistence boundaries or persistence technology are Reserved.
A new messaging, background-processing or distributed-caching infrastructure category is Reserved.
A new search, external-storage or external-identity infrastructure category is Reserved.
A major library or framework is Reserved.
Replacing an approved baseline technology is Reserved.
A project-wide convention or abstraction other code must follow (e.g. a project-wide Result model) is Reserved.
A new or changed authentication/authorization architecture is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
A changed project reference graph is Reserved.
A project-wide convention or abstraction other code must follow is Reserved.
Adopting API versioning is Reserved.

In an unclear case any 'yes' to the five questions (dependency/framework/infrastructure add-remove-replace, boundary change, new convention, observable behavior or contract change, expensive to reverse) makes the decision Reserved.
Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.
Completing an implementation is not a request to commit, push, merge or rewrite history.
Nullable reference types are enabled for every project.
Implicit global usings are enabled for every project.
.NET analyzers run at AnalysisLevel latest for every project.
EditorConfig code-style diagnostics are enforced during build.
The backend platform is .NET 10 LTS, C# 14, ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET Core Controllers; moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval.
.NET 10 is used on its latest stable servicing release.
FluentValidation is the standard library for explicit request and use-case validation.
Application code logs through ILogger<T> with Serilog (Serilog.AspNetCore) as the provider.
Serilog sinks are added only when required.
Do not use a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package without a concrete requirement.
Add Serilog sinks only when required; a Console sink is enough for local Development.
Testing uses NUnit; Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing with WebApplicationFactory<Program> is the integration-test baseline; backend test projects live under backend/ beside the production projects.
Testcontainers is used only when isolated real-provider tests justify it.

Angular baseline: the latest stable release supported by the selected Node.js, created with the current Angular CLI (compatible TypeScript and RxJS), standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless when supported, SCSS, Angular Material and CDK, Vitest.
No TypeScript upgrade beyond Angular's supported range and no obsolete directory structure imposed over the CLI's.
Conditional technologies are added only when their capability is needed.
Manual mapping for simple cases, Mapster when mapping volume warrants it, and no other mapping framework without approval.
The Microsoft resilience packages are added only when a real integration needs resilience.
