reviewer_text: Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers, incidental implementation constants or framework defaults the project has not intentionally overridden in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Product and task inputs are not instruction layers: they may request an engineering decision change but never silently override engineering policy; a conflicting request becomes a Decision Request.

Decisions are classified Decided/Delegated/Reserved; in an unclear case any 'yes' to the five questions (including removing a dependency or establishing a convention) makes it Reserved (reported tension with the Delegated class for local, behavior-neutral changes).

Raise a Reserved decision as a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) through architecture-decision; an explicit user instruction may count as approval but must be recorded there.
For changing the instruction system itself, ask the user to run /template-maintenance.
Nullable reference types and implicit usings are enabled repository-wide in Directory.Build.props.

Database string comparison follows the database/column collation; SQL Server defaults compare case-insensitively and accent-sensitively as a technology default, not an approved product semantic; changing the effective collation is a product decision.

Every leaf implementation must declare binds entries for frame-specific naming and project-layout vocabulary (reported broadly; the source says a leaf that must name a frame-specific project or directory declares a binds entry).
A replacement architecture frame must supply every role mapping and facet and review the embedded rules that use the frame's layer names.
The backend-testing slot contract makes facet metadata (framework, packages, case mechanism, fixture lifecycle, filter command) mandatory.
The backend-testing module's fixed adapter and competing-framework package lists determine which test frameworks are flagged (reported ambiguity).
The frontend module's hardcoded package and leak-token sets determine enforcement coverage; packages outside the sets are not checked (reported ambiguity).
Clearing the optional frontend selection requires removing its facet files and planning import.
A missing required capability facet or property is a conformance failure whose resolution requires a Decision Request.
The EF Core module states the property of one commit per use case (reported as possibly stronger than a commit boundary that allows justified multi-commit transactions).
Co-change detection uses concrete model and companion globs (Domain and Persistence/Configurations vs Seeding and Migrations), so model changes elsewhere produce no reminder (reported ambiguity).
A 201 response includes a Location header when a stable resource URI exists.
Once external clients rely on an API version, a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy (without a 'normally' qualifier).
Liveness must not depend on external dependencies whose unavailability could cause restart loops (a prohibition, not a 'normally avoid').
A singleton or hosted service that needs scoped work creates a scope per operation and resolves a scoped orchestration service.
Every VersionOverride needs a concrete, documented reason.
Treating typed exceptions as a consistent project-level decision may turn a single local typed exception into an architectural (Reserved-like) decision (reported ambiguity).
Expected outcomes such as not found or validation rejection are not logged as application errors.
NgModules are allowed for ordinary new features only when an integration or legacy dependency genuinely requires them (reported as a restriction stronger than a standalone default).
Use shared only for UI primitives or behavior that genuinely cross features; do not move feature code into shared merely because two components of one feature use it.
TimeProvider is used by default (not mandatorily) for current-time-dependent logic that needs deterministic tests.
Security-sensitive checks fail safely by default, without defined criteria for exceptions (reported ambiguity of 'by default').
The post-tool hook surfaces at most 25 diagnostics (reported risk of hiding later findings).
Shell-driven manifest-change checking compares against saved Git state (reported: no baseline outside Git).
Manifest or project-file changes caused by branch switches or other revision changes are exempt from the workflow reminder.
Post-tool checks block on WARN-level findings as well as errors after successful tool calls, while after failed calls findings are only added as context.
A PreToolUse payload without a tool name makes the shell guard fail closed.
Stop reminders are triggered by file-name heuristics (model files without seed/migration changes, production code without test changes) regardless of behavioral applicability.
Stop enforcement fires once per content fingerprint and skips active stop-hook calls rather than proving that requirements were resolved.
Hook failures must be reported to the user and repaired through the template-maintenance workflow.
Shell dependency commands depend on a Node-based PreToolUse gate and the hook wiring as an operational prerequisite.
The architecture check classifies project roles by naming and package markers (reported: custom-named projects become unknown).
Any project reference to a test project is an error, including references between test projects.
Forbidden-namespace enforcement only reads textual using directives with prefix matching, so fully qualified uses are missed and broad matches are possible.
Nested @-imports in instruction files other than CLAUDE.md are forbidden.
Implementation leak tokens are matched lexically across prose and examples, so a legitimate explanatory mention of another implementation can be blocked (reported ambiguity).
The CPM and version checks match literal text and do not evaluate effective MSBuild configuration (imports, conditions).
The npm checks cover only dependencies and devDependencies and selected version forms; other sections and tags are not flagged.
The shared checker library skips a fixed set of directories (reported: manifests there are never inspected).
Active instruction-root resolution uses the nearest instruction root within the Git boundary (reported scope ambiguity for nested trees).
Project references are read by a custom XML reader without full MSBuild condition/import semantics (reported divergence from effective references).
Co-change state derives from uncommitted Git files and Git-backed state storage (reported: committed task changes drop out of stop-hook scope).

Self-attested trailing comment markers (# add-dependency: checked, # peer-override: approved-by-user, # project-reference: checked) act as mandatory permission tokens for shell dependency and reference commands.
Dependency-command classification strips heredocs and parses shell lexically (reported: indirect installs are not recognized).
The peer-override check applies to npm, pnpm and yarn and to flag syntax regardless of value (e.g. --force=false is still treated as an override).
Dependency removal commands and project-reference operations also require workflow markers before they run.
Do not use floating versions such as '*', with no explicit-request exception (unlike prereleases).
Use computed for derived state and avoid unnecessary effect() when computed, template binding or explicit event handling is clearer.
ProblemDetails errors are mapped in one reusable place (interceptor plus parsing helper) and exposed as UI-friendly error state (phrased categorically, not 'when practical').
Compatible additions stay in the current API version.
Engineering decisions are recorded in the same change as a numbered ADR docs/decisions/NNNN-short-title.md with Status, Context, Decision and Consequences.
Any capability selection change or declared-property change requires an ADR and the user-invoked template-maintenance workflow.
The error-handling example maps request cancellation to status 499 (reported as a status choice beyond the cancellation rule).
Stopping when progress stalls creates a completion boundary broader than 'repeat until green or genuine user input' (reported ambiguity).
Add a distributed cache backend such as Redis only when deployment requirements justify it (distributed caching is Reserved).
Report review findings ordered by severity with severity, location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix, using the Critical/High/Medium/Low scale.
The JWT-validation example includes a minimum key length and an expiration bound (reported copy risk despite the numeric-example disclaimer).
Application services, repositories and external adapters use interface-to-implementation registration at architectural boundaries; concrete registration is fine for implementation-only helpers.
Prefer explicit registrations in small and medium projects; use assembly scanning only when registration volume creates genuine boilerplate, scanning the owning assembly.
ASP.NET Core Dockerfiles use a multi-stage build.
Docker changes are verified by building the image and checking startup, ports/configuration, non-root behavior when relevant, health probes, accidental secrets/files and meaningful tests.
Read time through TimeProvider and control it with FakeTimeProvider in tests.
Keep entity configuration separate with IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.
The EF Core mapping example embeds a numeric precision and an index without a local product-approval caveat (reported copy risk).
Paged queries must use a deterministic order, yet the skill's own sample orders only by a possibly non-unique timestamp (reported inconsistency).
Do not hide business behavior in persistence interceptors.
Without a repository convention, branch names use default prefixes such as feature/, fix/, refactor/, test/, docs/, chore/.
main, master and other protected branches are non-rewritable even when a force-push has been explicitly authorized (reported tension between the two sentences).
Destructive Git operations may be performed when explicitly requested or clearly required by an approved workflow (reported as broader than explicit request).
Health checks avoid Error-level logs for every normal failed probe.
An empty collection is a successful collection result returned as 200 with [], preferred over 204.
The Serilog bootstrap sample logs a fatal startup exception without rethrowing or setting a failure exit status (reported failure-visibility uncertainty).
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch is deprecated; use the official Elastic.Serilog.Sinks package.

Prefer platform trace identifiers; add an explicit correlation identifier only when required; validate or normalize an externally accepted identifier before propagating it; propagate correlation/tracing context across outbound calls.
Confirm the migration applies to a freshly created Development database before seeding.

Make each supporting type's role clear from its name or directory with established suffixes (Service, Dto, Request/Response, Result/Outcome, Validator, Rules/Policy, Factory, Mapper, Adapter) and avoid ambiguous names such as TaskWorkflow.
IntegrationTests references only the Api project; integration tests exercise Application, Infrastructure, persistence, routing, DI and serialization transitively through the Api host.

global.json pins the intended stable SDK line; when scaffolding select the current stable SDK for the target .NET release (no RC/preview SDK unless explicitly requested) and allow servicing through the chosen rollForward policy.

Project-reference commands are stopped until the project-structure procedure has been applied and the command is re-run with '# project-reference: checked'; a reference the layout prescribes follows the Decided layout, any other reference-graph change is Reserved and raised through architecture-decision first.
Use OWASP Top 10:2025 as an awareness taxonomy when it genuinely fits; not every issue needs a category; do not force an inaccurate mapping.

When API behavior changes, open the Development Swagger UI and confirm it loads, together with Controller/integration-test and response-metadata verification (X reads the Swagger UI step as applying to every API behavior change).

For every C# file created or modified by the task remove unused or redundant using directives, except imports needed for clarity or disambiguation; verify the changed files; no unrelated repository-wide using cleanup.
Other instructions use the slot contracts' stable role vocabulary instead of implementation names.
Implementation leak tokens appear only in the module's facets, manifest and the selection metadata.
A leaf that must name frame-specific projects or directories declares a binds entry in its manifest.
Placement belongs to the architecture frame and technique to the leaf capability.
Implementation-independent policy (framework-independent testing and frontend rules) stays outside the modules.
Test-project placement and the frontend workspace location belong to the frame; the persistence leaf binds to frame roles and does not decide placement.
Replacing a leaf replaces its facets (planning, rule facet, knowledge content, adapter data) without touching the framework-independent rules.
Clearing the optional frontend removes its facets and planning import with nothing else to change.
A persistence provider change edits only the declared provider-variant sections, the provider property and the declared string-comparison property.
A frame replacement supplies every role mapping and facet and reviews embedded rules that use the frame's layer names.
A slot implementation supplies every required facet, required property, required enforcement data and role mapping listed in its slot contract (checker-enforced).
A missing required facet or property is a conformance failure whose resolution requires a Decision Request.
The persistence implementation declares commit binding, migration mechanism, seeding mechanism, provider variant, observable string-comparison semantics and relational-testing expectations.
Replacing the persistence technology must not silently lose migration or seeding semantics.
A provider change is a provider-variant change inside the persistence slot, not a new slot.
MediatR and Kommand introduce a pattern listed as not adopted; adding them is a Reserved decision.
The manifest check flags MediatR and Kommand references.
In the executable manifest, integration tests may reference only the entry point project.
Core model and use-case layer code must not import Microsoft.AspNetCore or the persistence technology's namespaces.

NuGet and npm dependency additions and updates go through the add-dependency workflow first (need and approval check, package choice, latest stable compatible version, deprecation, vulnerability and license checks).
Dependency commands are denied until the identical command is re-run with the trailing comment '# add-dependency: checked' (self-certified marker; restore-only installs not gated).
Edited dependency entries trigger a reminder to confirm the add-dependency workflow was applied.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics: not 200 for every outcome, not 201 merely for an internal insert, not 202 for completed work.
A 201 response includes Location when a stable resource URI exists.
Application Services are the default orchestration mechanism for use cases (coordinating Domain objects, repositories, external-service abstractions and the Unit of Work).
A service becoming too large signals a responsibility review, not automatic adoption of another pattern.
Program.cs is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.
Controllers do not consume Infrastructure implementation types directly.
IUnitOfWork is the default commit boundary of an Application use case; repositories stage changes and do not commit independently; Application Services decide when to commit.
IUnitOfWork is implemented in Infrastructure over the scoped persistence session.
Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence session; repositories are injected explicitly.
IUnitOfWork must not act as a repository container or service locator.
For new code prefer file-scoped namespaces when consistent.
Keep one primary top-level type per file with a matching file name.
Use the Async suffix for Task/ValueTask-returning methods unless an existing contract or framework API would break.
Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked.
Avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work.
Do not reorganize an existing file merely to satisfy a preferred member ordering.

Use a regular constructor when validation or initialization is non-trivial, explicit fields help, the codebase uses that style, or parameter capture hurts readability; do not convert constructors mechanically.
Use records for value semantics and immutability and classes for identity, mutable lifecycle, inheritance or framework behavior; do not turn every DTO or Domain type into a record.
Keep implementation details non-public unless part of the public API; use sealed for deliberate non-inheritance intent, not as a speculative optimization.
Use standard .NET naming; private-field naming follows the repository convention.
Prefer strongly typed options for structured configuration consumed by services; direct IConfiguration access is appropriate in the composition root, provider setup and infrastructure registration.
Validate settings at startup when missing or invalid values prevent correct or secure operation.
NuGet Central Package Management: versions in Directory.Packages.props, versionless PackageReference entries by default, no duplicated central versions.
A VersionOverride needs a concrete, documented reason.
Package references live in the narrowest project that needs them.
Use npm by default unless the project deliberately adopts another package manager; build/test tooling goes into devDependencies unless there is a reason.
Maintain and commit package.json and package-lock.json.
Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when that improves clarity, using the simplest contract (null, bool, typed outcome, deliberately adopted Result<T>).
Do not force a generic Result<T> pattern.
Application outcome categories describe business semantics, not HTTP-named categories.
Expected outcomes are not logged as application errors.
Do not use exceptions casually for normal control flow.

Do not establish custom business exceptions as the default architecture or throw and catch merely to jump between normal branches; typed exceptions for selected cases are a consistent project-level decision.
Unexpected failures propagate to centralized handling at the outer boundary (IExceptionHandler); avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks.
Catch only to recover, translate, perform a defined fallback, add context or clean up.
Catch an exception only to recover, translate into the layer's own outcome, perform a defined fallback, add context while preserving the original exception, or perform cleanup.
Never swallow exceptions to continue execution.
Use a fallback only when its result is semantically acceptable; do not hide correctness failures behind convenient defaults.
Never swallow exceptions to continue execution.
Validate each concern at the owning layer, using FluentValidation for explicit request and use-case validation.

Api validates transport concerns, Application use-case and workflow rules, Domain genuine invariants (not moved into validators merely because the library is available), Infrastructure external-system assumptions.
Do not duplicate the same validation mechanically across layers.

Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access services; do not scatter HTTP calls through presentation components; use frontend API models matching the published contract and do not import backend Domain entities.
In Angular the data-access service is an @Injectable feature service using HttpClient.
Use the explicit form model for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation improves UX but does not replace backend validation, data-integrity or security enforcement.
The explicit form model is Angular Reactive Forms.
Frontend structure stays feature-oriented: a feature owns its UI and data-access logic; no application-wide technical buckets or empty architecture folders; core and shared stay small.
Use shared only for genuinely cross-feature primitives.

Compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, ArrayPool/MemoryPool, object pooling, custom serialization optimizations, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance are introduced only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.
Verify that allocation-oriented optimizations materially help.
EF Core is an adapter-layer implementation detail used directly inside the adapter layer, without crippling repositories to preserve a generic abstraction.
Do not leak EF Core concepts (DbContext/AppDbContext, DbSet<T>, EF APIs, EF-backed IQueryable<T>, query expressions, provider types) into the use-case layer.
Automatic development seeding runs only in the Development environment; never seed Production automatically.
Tests own their setup and do not use the development seeder.
Use normal NUnit conventions: [TestFixture] classes, [Test] for single scenarios, [SetUp]/[OneTimeSetUp] with matching teardown, Assert.That constraint assertions.
Explicit case tables are written as [TestCase] rows rather than TestCaseSource generators.
For small finite input or state spaces prefer explicit declarative cases over loops, branches, LINQ or generated case machinery, and state expected results instead of computing them.
Explicit cases are written as NUnit [TestCase] rows rather than TestCaseSource generators.

Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior; use integration tests when wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization, authentication or component interaction matters; no fixed ratio.
Prefer integration tests over reproducing real persistence or HTTP semantics with mocks.
Prefer one observable scenario per test; a multi-step test is appropriate when the sequence itself is the behavior.
Use fakes, stubs or mocks when they make an isolated test clearer; do not mock every dependency mechanically and do not forbid mocking project-owned abstractions.
Exactly four capability slots exist, three of them required.
The named workflow skills and embedded knowledge skills must exist.
The always-loaded budget is 6500 tokens.
Every instruction artifact starts with a one-line ownership header.
Instruction artifacts use no Level:/Kind: classification.
Rules stay flat in .claude/rules/ with non-empty paths.
The required workflow and embedded knowledge skills exist.
Skill frontmatter name equals the directory and the description is concrete.
Skill-private files live only under references/.
template-maintenance is user-only.
Only CLAUDE.md imports always-loaded files (no nested imports) and imports resolve.
File, workflow, skill and section references resolve (facet locations of a disabled optional slot are treated as inactive).
CLAUDE.md keeps a Workflow Routing section whose targets exist.
The map lists every instruction, enforcement and root configuration file.
The always-loaded surface stays within its token target (warning).
Every instruction file needs a one-line '> ' ownership header and no Level:/Kind: classification.
Rules stay flat in .claude/rules/ and declare a non-empty paths list.
Skill frontmatter name must equal the directory and the description must be concrete (at least 20 characters).
Skill-private files must live in the skill's references/ directory.
The code-reviewer agent must exist, disallow Write and Edit and preload the code-review workflow.
Exactly the four slots exist: architecture (required frame), persistence and backend-testing (required leaves) and frontend (optional leaf).
Each required slot has exactly one selected implementation and the optional slot zero or one; only selected implementations have runtime facets.
Contracts and manifests are maintainer metadata, not auto-loaded.
Exactly the four slots exist, each required slot has exactly one selected implementation and the optional slot is selected or disabled.
A selected module provides every required facet at its role-named location, every required property and every required enforcement entry.
A file declaring a Capability header must belong to a selected module and be listed in its manifest; unselected implementations must not enter runtime.
Planning facets are imported from CLAUDE.md exactly for the selected slots; an unselected slot's planning facet must not be imported or present.
settings.json must register exactly the expected hook events and scripts in exec form with matchers covering the listed tools.
Only the PreToolUse handler may (and must) set onFailure block; post-tool and Stop hooks must not set onFailure.
Hooks are wired in exec form (command node plus the script path through CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, no shell).
The critical PreToolUse hook fails closed (onFailure block) while post-tool and Stop hooks report failures visibly without blocking.
Failed shell commands are post-checked (PostToolUseFailure registration).
MAP.md must list every instruction, enforcement and root configuration file.
The checker warns when the always-loaded surface exceeds its fixed token budget.
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly and Polly.Extensions.Http are reported as errors whenever they appear in a manifest.
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch is reported as an error whenever it appears in a manifest.
FluentValidation.AspNetCore is reported as an error whenever it appears in a manifest.
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly and Polly.Extensions.Http produce categorical errors.
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch produces a categorical error.
FluentValidation.AspNetCore produces a categorical error.
Any PackageReference declaring a version in a project file is an error.
Test projects are recognized only by suffix, test-framework packages or IsTestProject.
Use the approved technology when one exists rather than silently selecting an alternative.
Replacing an approved technology is Reserved.
Direct Polly may be used only when a concrete requirement cannot be expressed through the Microsoft resilience APIs, and the reason must be documented.
Never add the deprecated Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly or Polly.Extensions.Http integrations.
Do not add deprecated or legacy automatic-validation integration packages merely to connect FluentValidation to the pipeline.
Permissive licenses commonly suitable for commercial use (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) may be accepted.

Do not install automatically a paid/commercial dependency or one with material obligations or unclassifiable licensing; explain the concern, present alternatives (say so when none exists) and do not silently substitute.
Do not draw legal conclusions beyond the published license information.
Use provider-based HttpClient configuration when configuration is required.
Do not introduce class-based interceptors without a reason.
When Angular Material is chosen use it consistently; do not add it automatically; do not wrap every component without a concrete reason.
Keep adopted OpenAPI-generated client code separate and regenerate it when the contract changes.
Frontend tests target meaningful behavior, validation, data-access mapping, route/auth and complex state, not framework internals; E2E for a few important workflows; no duplication across levels.
Create the workspace under frontend/<Name>.Web/ with the current Angular CLI and the baseline (standalone, strict, routing, SCSS, zoneless when supported, CLI Vitest setup).
Unit and component tests stay colocated; Playwright E2E tests, when required, live under frontend/<Name>.Web/e2e/.
Build and test the frontend through the scripts the workspace actually defines; never invent npm scripts.
In CI use npm ci when a maintained lockfile supports it.

Accepted architecture, stack, convention or public-contract decisions are recorded in the same change as an ADR docs/decisions/NNNN-short-title.md (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences) and in the affected decision record.
A rejected request is recorded only when the rejection itself is a durable decision.
Register FluentValidation validators with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions.
Follow the project's established validation invocation pattern rather than a second competing mechanism.
Choose the authentication scheme by application type (Bearer/OIDC for SPA to API, cookies for server-rendered apps, Identity for owned local accounts, external OIDC/OAuth for delegated identity).
Do not issue custom JWTs when an existing identity provider already owns token issuance.
Use stable constants for policy names repeated across the application.
Prefer a policy over scattered compound role strings when several roles or claims represent one capability.
Reproduce the actual failure with the narrowest command before editing.
Read the complete output, group errors by root cause and fix the highest-leverage cause first.
For failing tests decide whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentional contract change is at fault.
Determine the authoritative contract for cross-stack failures.
Update obsolete APIs from verified documentation, never fabricated.
Keep repair iterations small and bounded: rerun the narrowest failing verification after each meaningful fix and expand only after the focused failure is resolved.
Do not run unrelated build systems.
Stop when progress stalls.
Do not repeat variants of a failed guess.
Do not weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests or compiler, analyzer, TypeScript or lint failures to make verification pass.
No strong-to-weak assertion swaps, any-casts, disabled strict mode or suppressed template diagnostics.
Update a test only for an intentionally requested contract change.

A build fix must not bypass architecture to compile (Application to Infrastructure references, persistence-technology types in Application, business logic in Controllers, frontend-only authorization, HTTP calls scattered into components).
Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing.
When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine user input is required.
Never claim the problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains.
Never leave the repository knowingly worse; unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.
Report an unavailable toolchain instead of editing source or changing declared SDK/Node/framework versions.
The build-fix report states the initial failure, root cause, changes made and remaining issues.
The build-fix report states backend build, frontend build and tests as PASS, NOT RUN or NOT APPLICABLE.
CI pipelines reproduce the repository's supported build and test commands.
Inspect the repository first and do not assume a database, Redis, Docker or frontend tooling.
Add stages for the actual project rather than generic boilerplate.
Do not hardcode a database provider into a generic pipeline.
Do not make an unadopted formatter a mandatory CI gate.
Do not depend on developer-machine state.
Keep pipeline failures visible.
Prefer promoting the same tested artifact or image through environments over recompiling per environment.
Prefer workload/federated identity over long-lived deployment credentials when supported.
Code review identifies concrete defects and risks in the actual changed behavior.

Review priorities are correctness, security/authorization, data integrity/persistence, architecture boundaries, concurrency/integration, missing meaningful tests, maintainability and credible performance; style preferences are not elevated above behavioral defects.
Code is not reported as a violation merely for differing from an unadopted pattern.
Before judging, the review reads the changed code with enough surrounding code (callers, contracts, dependencies); no review of isolated lines.
The review reads the owning rules and knowledge skills of every changed area before judging conformance.
No review findings for failures without a plausible execution path.
No findings merely to populate categories; when there are no meaningful findings say so and name important areas that could not be verified.
Tool output is evidence rather than authority.
No filler praise.
Record an approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value under a stable setting name.

When an approved value is added, changed or removed, identify and update every affected surface (old value and name, validators and DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, database mapping, frontend validation and UI hints, tests and test data, documentation and examples, mirrored configuration).
Update only affected behavior.
Search for stale references, build, test and run verify.
One changed literal does not establish synchronization.
Inspect the relevant existing code before a non-trivial change and apply the governing rules and skills.
For greenfield work or unopened files read the owning rules explicitly before writing code.
Create test projects with dotnet new nunit at the locations project-structure defines and remove duplicated build properties and package versions.

Test packages through add-dependency: NUnit, NUnit3TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing for integration tests, Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing when FakeTimeProvider is needed.
Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.
Do not automatically stash, reset or discard work to make a merge or rebase proceed.
Do not remove a worktree that contains uncommitted user work.
Before a repository-changing Git operation inspect the relevant repository state (status, diff, staged diff).
Use the minimum operation required and do not silently clean up unrelated working-tree changes.
Do not perform unnecessary operations such as renaming an existing user branch to satisfy a naming convention.
Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the intended logical change; do not stage unrelated files merely because they are modified.
One logical change per commit with its protecting tests; no artificial tiny commits.
Do not combine unrelated fixes into one commit.
Parallel implementation streams use separate branches or worktrees and each worktree stays focused on its branch's concern.
One branch is not checked out in multiple normal worktrees.
Prefer one logical change per commit with implementation and its tests together; no artificial tiny commits.
Follow the repository commit-message convention, otherwise Conventional Commits.
main, master and other protected or shared branches are treated as non-rewritable.
A shared branch is never force-pushed unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting and the consequences are understood.
406 when no acceptable response representation can be produced; not to be confused with 415.
415 when the request representation is unsupported; 415 concerns the request body format and 406 the response format.
422 for structurally valid but semantically invalid requests; follow an established 400-for-both convention; new APIs that distinguish them use 400 for contract errors and 422 for semantics.
428 when a contract-required precondition is missing; other mandatory preconditions only when the contract defines them.
429 for rate-limited requests with Retry-After when the retry time is known; validation failures are not represented as rate limiting.
502 only when this API is an intermediary receiving an invalid upstream response; not every dependency failure.
503 when the service is temporarily unable to handle the request, with Retry-After when a meaningful retry time is known.
504 only for an upstream timeout when this API is an intermediary; distinguish client cancellation, own timeouts and upstream timeouts.
Repeated POSTs that must not duplicate effects may use an Idempotency-Key; key reuse with a different payload is 409; idempotency is not claimed merely because duplicates are unlikely.
When HTTP-level optimistic concurrency is part of the contract prefer standard conditional semantics (ETag, If-Match, 412) and do not replace them with custom status codes.
Prefer System.Net.Http.Json / System.Text.Json where sufficient, with explicit serialization options when the external contract differs from the application's defaults.
Do not reuse internal Domain entities as remote API contracts to avoid mapping.
Use hedging only for operations safe to execute multiple times; do not hedge state-changing operations.
Do not wrap normal persistence operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; prefer the provider's execution strategy when it supports transient retry.

Treat EF Core migrations as source code and review every generated migration before committing it (destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys, delete behavior).
Do not casually alter existing migrations; regenerate or edit an uncommitted migration only when that matches the project's migration workflow.
Whenever Domain or persistence changes affect seeded entities, update the development DbSeeder in the same change and review it together with the corresponding migration.
Recreating the Development database at any revision yields valid representative seed data; already seeded rows of an existing database are not patched.
Build the affected projects and run the relevant tests for the change.
For persistence changes run the persistence and integration tests.
For persistence changes confirm the migration applies to a freshly created Development database before seeding.
Reserved decisions require explicit approval.
Changing an accepted project or architecture decision, including a capability selection, is Reserved.

Adopting a new architectural style or pattern (CQRS, mediator, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices, Rich Domain Model or systematic DDD tactical patterns, project-wide Result model) is Reserved.
Adding a production project, layer or assembly is Reserved.
Changing persistence boundaries (including multiple contexts) or persistence technology is Reserved.
Adding a messaging, background processing or distributed caching infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a search, external storage or external identity infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a major library or framework is Reserved.
Replacing an approved baseline technology is Reserved.
Introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction is Reserved.
Changing the authentication/authorization architecture is Reserved.
Making a breaking public API change is Reserved.
Investigation prompts are not automatic vulnerability declarations; do not invent exploitability.
Rate severity by reachability, exposure and exploitability rather than mechanically by pattern, CVSS or OWASP category.
Avoid known false positives.
Mark findings with incomplete evidence as needing verification.
Do not claim a static scan proves design security.
Do not upgrade packages during a scan unless asked.
Security review does not require a specific MCP server, agent, analyzer, commercial scanner or external tool; available tooling is evidence, not the sole authority.
A scanner-reported issue is reported only after inspecting the actual code and its reachability.
Confirmed security findings are reported in a fixed shape: severity tag, file:line location and title, OWASP category, Evidence, Impact and Remediation.
Findings with incomplete evidence use the NEEDS VERIFICATION form stating what effective behavior depends on.
Read .claude/MAP.md first when maintaining the instruction system.

Place new content by kind (planning-time governance in the compact CLAUDE.md, stack in technology-stack, capability decisions in docs/capabilities, path rules in flat .claude/rules with paths, procedures in workflow skills, technique in knowledge skills or references, mechanical checks in hooks/scripts wired in settings.json, slot metadata in CONTRACT.md/MODULE.md).
Keep each policy's trigger role.
Never hide a must/must-not rule only inside a knowledge skill or private reference.
Keep the always-loaded surface compact.
Update MAP.md.
Change a rule at its single authoritative owner and use pointers elsewhere; never restate a rule in a second place.
Keep each policy's trigger role: planning-time policy on the always-loaded surface, path policy in a path rule covering its full scope, procedural obligations in their workflow.
Do not hide a must/must-not rule only inside a knowledge skill or a private reference.
Update .claude/MAP.md and run check-instructions.js, fixing every error.
Verification starts with the final changed-file set and diff: the change matches the requested scope without unrelated refactoring and no generated/build artifacts or secrets were added.
Temporary diagnostics and probes are removed only after their behavior is preserved.
The final diff is reviewed after all fixes for unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, unintended TODO/FIXME, stale temporary tests or scripts and architecture drift.
The final diff has no unapproved drift from the product sources and no stale surfaces after a settings change.
All files use UTF-8, a final newline, trimmed trailing whitespace and 4-space indentation by default.
JSON/YAML/Markdown, TS/HTML/SCSS/CSS and project/XML files use 2-space indentation.
File-scoped namespaces suggested; System usings sorted first without separated import groups; unused usings (IDE0005) at suggestion severity.
var when the type is apparent; explicit types for built-in types and elsewhere (suggestion).
Modern syntax preferences (primary constructors, collection and switch expressions, pattern matching) are silent so working code is not modernized mechanically.
Braces preferred (suggestion); expression-bodied methods off and properties on (silent).
PascalCase for types and members, I-prefixed PascalCase interfaces, camelCase parameters and locals (suggestion).
If an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable product behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Defining product behavior not defined by product sources is Reserved.

Role map: core model <Name>.Domain; use-case layer <Name>.Application with Application Services; persistence contract a specific repository interface in Application; commit boundary IUnitOfWork in Application implemented in Infrastructure; adapter layer <Name>.Infrastructure; entry point a Controller in <Name>.Api; composition root Program.cs.
Test projects are <Name>.Application.Tests and <Name>.IntegrationTests; <Name>.Domain.Tests or <Name>.Infrastructure.Tests only when justified.
Each required slot has exactly one selected implementation and the optional slot zero or one; only selected implementations have runtime facets.

The capability slots are architecture (required frame), persistence and backend-testing (required leaves) and frontend (optional leaf), selected as clean-architecture, ef-core (provider sqlserver), nunit and angular.
Use the latest stable servicing release of the .NET 10 LTS line.
global.json pins the stable SDK line.
FluentValidation is the standard library for explicit request and use-case validation.
Application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog (Serilog.AspNetCore) as the provider.
Logging sinks are added only when required.
