reviewer_text: Engineering policy lives in the instruction system; a more volatile level may refine a more stable level but must not contradict it, and a contradiction is reported instead of resolved locally.

Normative vocabulary: must/must-not violations are defects; deviation from a default needs a concrete reason and must be reported; prefer/avoid are guidance; requires approval marks a Reserved decision.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior do not require approval (marked as a default).

Decided/Delegated/Reserved classification with a Reserved list including reference-graph changes, and an unclear-case test in which any dependency addition or removal makes a choice Reserved (reported tension with Delegated local changes).

Run the matching named workflow (development-workflow, project-structure, verify, build-fix, code-review, add-dependency, custom-settings, architecture-decision, delivery-pipeline, security-scan, git-workflow) instead of improvising a procedure.
All files use UTF-8, a final newline, trimmed trailing whitespace (not for Markdown) and 4-space indentation, with 2 spaces for JSON/YAML/TS/HTML/CSS/JS and MSBuild/XML files.

Local secret and configuration overrides (.env, .env.* except .env.example, appsettings.*.local.json) and Claude local settings are git-ignored (reported risk of hiding intentionally maintained configuration).
Log an unexpected exception once, at the boundary that handles it; do not log it again in every layer it passes through.
The technology-neutral runtime rule file loads only for backend C# paths (reported: frontend runtime work lacks automatic coverage).
The security rule file's path globs omit standalone scripts and unlisted configuration formats (reported trigger gap).

Configure CORS to the narrowest policy satisfying actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with unrestricted origins (reported: the line's default marker may be read as qualifying the never clause).
Automatic test-rule loading depends on Tests naming, .spec.ts files or an e2e folder (reported trigger gap).

Name supporting types so their architectural role is clear from the type name and/or its directory (prefer); split a feature into responsibility-specific subdirectories only when a flat directory becomes hard to navigate.
Once external clients rely on an API version, avoid silent breaking changes; a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
Catch an exception only to recover, translate it into the layer's own outcome, perform a defined fallback, add useful context or clean up; do not swallow failures to continue.
Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or any other generic CRUD contract; a generic repository or base class may exist only as an Infrastructure implementation detail.
Use TimeProvider for application logic that depends on the current clock and needs deterministic testing (marked default); do not mechanically replace explicit or stored timestamps.
Entity mappings live in Infrastructure as IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> classes (prefer).

Test projects are <Name>.Application.Tests, <Name>.IntegrationTests and optional <Name>.Domain.Tests / <Name>.Infrastructure.Tests with fixed references; frontend unit/component tests are colocated in the workspace and E2E tests live under frontend/<Name>.Web/e2e/.

Package versions belong in Directory.Packages.props, project PackageReference entries are versionless, a VersionOverride requires a concrete reported reason, and centrally managed versions are not duplicated in .csproj files.
Bash/PowerShell calls run the pre-bash hook through node with a 30-second timeout and onFailure block (fail closed).
When a shell call cannot be checked (unreadable payload, missing command or unavailable infrastructure) the pre-shell hook fails closed and blocks it.
Peer-bypass detection matches --force, -f and --legacy-peer-deps (incl. =true) and npm_config_force / npm_config_legacy_peer_deps environment assignments.
Shell tokenization in the pre-bash hook does not distinguish comments or heredoc content from executable commands (reported false positives).
Nested-shell parsing is depth-limited and does not inspect script or encoded-command contents (reported: indirect overrides escape the guard).
Git manifest discovery excludes ignored files and the unborn-branch baseline treats existing manifests as unchanged (reported missing delta reminder).
Outside a Git work tree, manifest validation after a shell call runs only after a recognized dependency command that did not fail.
After editing CLAUDE.md or .claude/**/*.{md,json,mjs} the instruction-structure check runs, using the active root's checker or, when it is missing there, the launcher repository's checker.
Co-change detection uses regexes that assume exact project and directory names (reported missed seeder reminders).
The Stop-hook digest includes only the first 500 sorted relevant files (reported missed re-reminders).

At Stop, filename-based co-change reminders (model without seeder, migrations, production code without tests, CUSTOM_SETTINGS) must be addressed or explained; repeats are suppressed by a fingerprint of changed files and content.
Review-list exceptions are honored when the package name appears anywhere in an '## Accepted' section of decisions.md or overview.md (substring match, without interpreting approval or rejection).
The manifest check infers project roles from names and reads MSBuild XML without evaluation (reported accuracy limits for conditional and property-expanded references).
Central Package Management is recognized only as a literal unqualified switch in the inspected file (reported false 'missing CPM' for imported settings).
The NuGet version check flags empty versions, versions containing '*' and the prerelease suffixes alpha, beta, preview, rc, dev, nightly and pre (allowed only when explicitly requested).
Reference-direction checks skip test projects and projects without a recognized layer.
npm manifest validation covers only dependencies and devDependencies with fixed floating-version, review-list and tooling patterns, and flags .npmrc peer-dependency bypass settings.
npm delta extraction omits optionalDependencies and collapses repeated section declarations by package ID (reported missed deltas).
Centralize ProblemDetails parsing/mapping (e.g. an error interceptor or mapping service) and branch on stable codes or fields, not message text.
The error-handling example maps request cancellation to status 499 (reported as a status choice beyond the cancellation rule).
If the project deliberately adopts a Result pattern, use it consistently with typed errors rather than strings.
Prefer policies when authorization is more than a trivial role check, keep repeated policy names in stable constants, and use roles when the business model is genuinely role-oriented.
Stop when progress has clearly stalled rather than making speculative edits (reported: this may end work before green or before genuine user input is needed).
HybridCache is optional; add a distributed backend such as Redis only when deployment requires it.
Mutations follow the normal repository/Unit of Work flow and the affected cache entry is removed or updated after the commit succeeded; HybridCache stays behind the abstraction.
Report review findings ordered by severity with severity, file/location, problem, why it matters and smallest reasonable fix, on the scale Critical, High, Medium, Low.
Use a stable descriptive setting name and record the value and its purpose in the table.
When the project deploys containers use multi-stage builds, explicit project-file copy for restore caching, runtime configuration supplied at run time and health probes.
Use interface-to-implementation registration at architectural boundaries (Application services, repositories, external adapters); concrete registration is fine for implementation-only helpers.
The EF Core mapping example embeds a monetary precision and an index without a local product-approval caveat (reported copy risk).
Paged queries need a deterministic order, yet the skill's example orders only by a possibly non-unique CreatedAt (reported inconsistency).
When the required seed graph is complex, ask the task to describe the dataset instead of inventing a large generic graph.
main, master and other protected/shared branches are treated as non-rewritable, stated alongside the explicit-request exception for force-pushing a shared branch (reported tension).
Destructive Git operations may be performed when explicitly requested or clearly required by an approved workflow (reported as broader than an explicit request).
Use DelegatingHandler for genuine HTTP pipeline concerns (access-token acquisition, correlation propagation, request signing), never for business decisions.
The Serilog bootstrap example logs a fatal startup failure without rethrowing or setting a failure exit status (reported failure-visibility uncertainty).
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch is deprecated; use the official Elastic.Serilog.Sinks package.
The C# property example trims and rejects whitespace silently (reported copy risk for unapproved string semantics).

Make supporting-type roles clear by name/directory with established suffixes (Service, Dto, Request/Response, Result/Outcome, Validator, Rules/Policy, Factory, Mapper, Adapter), prefer unambiguous names over TaskWorkflow and avoid generic Models/Helpers/Common/Utils buckets.

global.json pins the intended SDK line; select the current stable SDK of the target release at scaffolding time with a roll-forward policy allowing normal servicing (the example version is illustrative).
Never add Production credentials or Production migration automation while scaffolding (reported as broader than prohibiting startup migrations by default).
Every security report states that static review cannot prove the application secure and may miss runtime-only and other vulnerability classes.

Security review uses seven layers (dependencies, secrets/configuration, injection, authentication/access control, browser/HTTP, sensitive data/logging/errors, exceptional conditions) with typical OWASP Top 10:2025 mappings.
Swagger examples and descriptions never show exception types, stack traces, SQL, connection strings or file paths.
After API changes open the Development Swagger UI (together with controller/integration-test and metadata verification); X reads the Swagger UI step as applying to every API change.
Run template-maintenance only when the user invokes it; never start it automatically.

Hook registrations must use exec form (command node with [launcher, event] args), a positive timeout, a literal handler map with known events and the required registrations; onFailure block is required on and reserved for the PreToolUse guard.
The code-reviewer's read-only role is expressed only as a deny list of Write, Edit and NotebookEdit; shell and other mutation-capable tools are not mechanically excluded.

Replacing a technology edits its Level 2 module, the Level 3 selection and the embedding workflows/assets while Levels 0 and 1 stay unchanged (reported: boundary-changing replacements may need edits there).
For every created or modified C# file remove unused or redundant using directives, except those needed for clarity or disambiguation; verify the changed files; no repository-wide cleanup.
Every instruction artifact carries a header (Level, Owns, Scope, Loads, Depends on).
Rules live in level directories with paths front matter.
Conformance dependencies ('Depends on') point only to the same or a more stable level, without cycles.
Levels 0 and 1 name no concrete technology beyond .NET, C#, TypeScript (Git for repository safety).
Every instruction artifact is listed in the instruction map.
After editing CLAUDE.md or .claude/**/*.{md,json,mjs} the structure checker runs and every reported error must be fixed.
Peer-dependency bypass commands are blocked; if the user explicitly decides to override, the user runs the command.
Every project-reference shell command is blocked, even for approved changes; mapped references follow project-structure and other graph changes need a Decision Request through architecture-decision.

Every 'dotnet add/remove ... reference' and 'dotnet reference add/remove' command is blocked before it runs; references mapped by layout.md follow project-structure, any other reference-graph change needs a Decision Request (architecture-decision) and an approved change is applied in the project file.
Every added or removed ProjectReference and every added, moved or removed project file is reported for confirmation against the layout or an approved decision and must be reported.

When SPECIFICATION.md or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md is edited, keep the two consistent; CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes run custom-settings; approved behavior changes follow development-workflow (PostToolUse reminder).
At Stop, a changed CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md prompts running custom-settings to synchronize every affected surface (once per change state).
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly, Polly.Extensions.Http and Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch are deny-listed packages that must not be added.
Polly, MediatR, Kommand, AutoMapper and FluentValidation.AspNetCore need an approved decision or a reported reason before they are added.
PackageReference entries carry no Version.
A VersionOverride needs a reported concrete reason.
ManagePackageVersionsCentrally stays true in Directory.Packages.props.
Keep each dependency in the narrowest project or workspace that actually requires it.
Remove a dependency that the current change makes unused when doing so is safe to verify; do not perform unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrowly scoped task.
Tests verify observable behavior so that they survive internal refactoring; no unnecessary dependence on private methods, call sequences or implementation details.
When provider behavior matters, test against the actual database provider; never claim provider fidelity from a test on a different provider (default).
Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful.
Frontend validation improves UX but never replaces backend validation or data-integrity and security enforcement.
Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when useful (null, bool, a typed outcome or a deliberately adopted Result model) with the simplest contract.
Do not force a generic Result<T> pattern; no HTTP-named outcome categories in Application; describe Application semantics and map them to HTTP in Api.
Unexpected failures propagate to centralized boundary handling (IExceptionHandler with AddProblemDetails/UseExceptionHandler); avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks.
Catch only to recover, translate, perform a defined fallback, add context or clean up; do not swallow failures.

Validate each concern at the owning layer: Api transport and request-contract concerns, Application use-case and straightforward workflow rules, Domain genuine invariants, Infrastructure external-system assumptions.
No mechanical duplication of a rule across layers and no Domain invariants moved into request validators.

Backend Clean Architecture with four layers and inward dependencies (Domain business concepts; Application use-case orchestration and inward abstractions; Infrastructure persistence and external-service implementations; Api entry points and composition root).
The frontend is a separate client workspace that communicates with the backend only through the published HTTP API and is organized by feature.
Reviews prioritize real defects (correctness, security, data integrity, architecture, concurrency/integration, meaningful tests, maintainability, credible performance) over style.
Reviews must not require or enforce patterns the architecture has not adopted.

The persistence framework is an Infrastructure implementation detail: use it normally inside Infrastructure (concrete repositories may use the full EF Core API) but do not leak its concepts into Application.
Do not cripple repository implementations to preserve a generic abstraction.
Api entry points are ASP.NET Core Controllers; Minimal API endpoint groups only when explicitly requested.

IActionResult, ActionResult<T>, ProblemDetails, HttpContext, ClaimsPrincipal, IHttpContextAccessor and StatusCodes are transport types that belong to Api and never appear in Application or Domain contracts.
Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation failures with stable, safe machine-readable fields (default).
Centralized handling of unexpected exceptions uses IExceptionHandler with AddProblemDetails() / UseExceptionHandler().
Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is appropriate.
Do not treat ASP.NET Core Data Protection as universal database encryption.
Production containers use an appropriate runtime image (the ASP.NET runtime image) rather than the SDK image for convenience and do not switch to root to bypass permission problems.
Production containers run as the image's non-root user where supported.
Keep build tooling out of runtime images.
Keep environment configuration external.
Production containers run as the image's non-root user where supported.
Keep environment configuration external to container images.
Use WebApplicationFactory<Program>-based integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication/authorization, DI, repositories, EF Core or persistence is the subject (default).
Integration tests run in an environment named Testing with isolated test resources.
Tests are deterministic, independent of execution order and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state.
The Testing environment uses isolated resources.
When provider behavior matters, test against the actual database provider; never claim provider fidelity from a test running on a different provider.
EF Core InMemory is not relational and never verifies relational or SQL Server behavior.
IUnitOfWork is the normal commit boundary of an Application use case: repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit.
The Infrastructure IUnitOfWork implementation delegates to the shared scoped DbContext.
FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library.
Application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog as provider.
Application-level validators live in Application and are registered with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions from Application's own registration.

Follow the project's established validation invocation pattern rather than a second competing mechanism; do not adopt a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration without a concrete requirement.
Substantial seed construction lives in a dedicated internal DbSeeder invoked through a narrow Infrastructure initialization extension.
Automatic development seeding runs only in Development, never in Production; tests own their setup and never use the seeder.
Backend platform: .NET 10 LTS (latest stable servicing release), C# 14, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET Core Controllers; a preview/RC move requires approval.
Validation uses FluentValidation with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions; logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog.AspNetCore as provider.
Mapster (with Mapster.DependencyInjection) is added only when mapping volume is repetitive or non-trivial; manual mapping is fine for simple cases.
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience / Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience are added only when a real integration needs resilience.
Adding another mapping framework requires approval (alongside mediator libraries not being adopted).
Physical layout: backend production and test projects under backend/<Name>.<Layer>/, the Angular workspace under frontend/<Name>.Web/, documentation under docs/; no top-level tests/ directory.

Before installation check that the exact selected version is not deprecated, review known vulnerability information and verify its license from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary).
Permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) may normally be accepted; a free download does not make a package acceptable.
Check deprecation, known vulnerabilities and license of the exact selected version from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary).
Permissive licenses are normally acceptable.

Do not automatically install a paid/commercial dependency or one with a materially restrictive or unclassifiable license; explain the concern and present options (say so when no free alternative exists) without silently substituting.
No legal conclusions beyond the published license.
When resilience is required prefer the Microsoft resilience packages; the named Polly integrations are not used.
Never use npm --force or --legacy-peer-deps merely to bypass incompatible peer dependencies; the project hook blocks these and an explicitly approved override is run by the user.
Report the package, version, license, reason and checks performed.
Removing a dependency removes the reference and its central version when no project uses it any more, then rebuilds and runs the affected tests.
A feature owns its UI and frontend data access; do not move feature code to shared just because two components use it; shared holds genuinely cross-feature primitives.
Use computed for derived state; avoid effect() when computed, a template binding or an event handler expresses the dependency more clearly.
When the project uses Angular Material, use it consistently for common UI primitives; do not wrap every Material component in a custom abstraction without a concrete reason.
Generated OpenAPI clients are treated as generated: kept separate from handwritten feature logic, regenerated when the contract changes and not patched.
Frontend E2E focuses on a small number of important workflows unless broader coverage is required.
Delegated decisions taken are mentioned in the report.
A rejected Decision Request is not recorded as a decision but is mentioned in the report.
Delegated choices proceed and are mentioned in the report.

A Decision Request contains Context, Options (normally two or three, including the smallest change, each with consequences, cost to reverse and affected levels/files), Recommendation, Blocked and Proceeding with.
After approval, in the same change, add an entry to the matching decision summary (architecture-level in overview.md, project/stack in decisions.md) and update the owning rule module.
A rejected request is not recorded as a decision; mention it in the report.

Catch only to recover, translate to an abstraction-level outcome, perform cleanup that cannot be expressed otherwise or add context preserving the original; swallowed failures and catch/log/rethrow at every layer are anti-patterns.
Expected outcomes (NotFound, validation failures, rejected operations) are normally not logged as errors.

Choose the authentication scheme by application type: Bearer/OIDC for an SPA calling an API, cookies for server-rendered apps, ASP.NET Core Identity for owned local accounts, an external OIDC/OAuth provider when identity is delegated.
Do not issue custom JWTs when the delegated identity provider already issues tokens.
Build-fix starts by reproducing the failure with the narrowest command.
Read the complete output, group errors by root cause and fix the highest-leverage cause first.
For failing tests decide whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentional contract change is at fault.
Determine the authoritative contract instead of patching both sides of a cross-stack break.
Update obsolete APIs from verified documentation, never invented.
Repair in small bounded iterations: rerun the narrowest failing verification after each meaningful fix and expand only after the focused failure is resolved.
Do not run unrelated build systems.
Use several focused attempts rather than an unlimited loop.
Stop when progress stalls instead of making speculative edits.

Never weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests or compiler, TypeScript, lint or analyzer failures to make verification pass (no strong-to-weak assertion swaps, no any-casts or disabled strict mode).
Update a test only for an intentionally requested contract change.

A green build obtained by violating the architecture (outward or invalid project references, persistence types in Application, business logic in Controllers, Angular-only authorization, HTTP calls scattered into components) is not a successful repair.
Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing.
Use frontend scripts and runners that actually exist (inspect package.json instead of assuming a command); never invent npm scripts.
In CI use npm ci when a maintained lockfile supports it and do not reflexively replace lockfile-based installs.
When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine user input is required.
Never claim a problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains.
Never leave the repository knowingly worse; unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.
When the required toolchain is unavailable report the limitation instead of editing source or changing declared SDK/Node/framework versions.
Never invent failures without a plausible execution path.
Never invent review findings to populate categories; when there are no meaningful findings say so and state the important areas that could not be verified.
Run the full security-scan only when the user requested a security audit, the change is materially security-sensitive, or a concrete finding justifies broader investigation.
Run architecture, formatting/analyzer, dependency and security checks according to the change's risk.

When a CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value is added, changed or removed, search for and update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored surface; changing one literal alone does not establish synchronization.
Backend validation stays authoritative and frontend validation is kept in sync for UX.
Search for stale references and run the normal verification.

CI definitions stay in source control, reproduce the repository's supported build and test commands for the parts that actually exist and never hide build or test failures (no continue-on-error on build/test steps, no suppressed exit codes, no skipped failing tests).
Formatting/analyzer gates only when adopted.
CI restores from a clean environment without developer-machine state.

CI definitions stay in source control, reproduce the supported build and test commands and never hide build or test failures (no continue-on-error on build/test steps, no suppressed exit codes, no skipped failing tests).
Backend CI flow: dotnet restore, then dotnet build --no-restore --configuration Release, then dotnet test --no-build --configuration Release.
CI does not upgrade packages automatically unless the project adopted automated dependency updates.
Do not apply production database migrations automatically from normal application startup (in containers or anywhere else).
Production migration is an explicit, visible deployment step at a controlled point with approved credentials.
Deployment never runs Development seeding in Production.
CI and CD may be separate; use environment protection/approval where supported and promote the same tested artifact with runtime configuration differences.

Verify the pipeline (clean restore, builds, configured tests, no developer state, no secrets, expected artifacts) and, for containers, image build, startup, ports/configuration, non-root behavior, health probes and no stray secrets/files.
Prefer explicit registrations in small and medium projects; scan when registration volume creates genuine boilerplate, scanning the assembly that owns the services.
A singleton or hosted service needing scoped work creates a scope per operation and resolves a scoped orchestration service, not Infrastructure internals.
Inspect relevant existing code before non-trivial changes and apply the applicable rules.
Workflows explicitly read the rule files they depend on because path rules may not have fired (for example in a new repository).
Schema changes are created as new EF Core migrations from the Infrastructure project with the Api project as startup project.
Changed behavior gets maintained automated coverage at the right level.
The development-workflow report summarizes what changed, the verify result block and remaining known issues.
The report lists unresolved Decision Requests.
Use tracking queries when loaded entities are modified and committed through the current Unit of Work and AsNoTracking() for read-only entity queries.
Avoid lazy loading by default; prefer an explicit query shape.
EF.CompileAsyncQuery helps only on a measured hot path where compilation/cache lookup is material.
Interceptors suit infrastructure cross-cutting behavior such as auditing, not hidden business behavior.
Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.
Never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work.
Do not automatically stash, reset or discard local work for a merge or rebase.
Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (status, diffs) and use the minimum operation required; do not silently clean up unrelated working-tree changes.
Before a high-risk operation inspect what it would lose or rewrite.
Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the requested logical change; do not stage unrelated modified files.
One logical change per commit with its tests; no artificial tiny commits or combined unrelated fixes.
Before pushing confirm branch and state, ensure relevant verification completed and avoid pushing unrelated local commits.
Follow the repository's commit-message convention; otherwise Conventional Commits are a useful default.
Follow an existing branch-naming convention; otherwise prefixes such as feature/, fix/, refactor/, test/, docs/, chore/ with meaningful names.
Use separate branches and worktrees for parallel implementation streams; one branch is not checked out in several normal worktrees; keep each worktree focused.
Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete or rename branches or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.
Never force-push a shared branch unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting.
A database health check is a lightweight connectivity/availability check without business queries, large scans or writes.
Keep probe responses small; detailed diagnostics only on a protected endpoint.
Avoid Error-level logs for every normal failed probe.
For repeated DELETE of an absent resource choose one convention (204 or 404) and use it consistently.
304 only for a conditional request whose cached representation is still valid, not a business 'nothing changed'.
400 for malformed JSON, invalid shape, binding failures and missing transport-level input; not for authentication failure.
406 when no acceptable representation can be produced; 415 for an unsupported request media type.
422 for structurally valid but semantically invalid requests, or 400 for both when the project deliberately uses it; follow the established convention.
428 when a contract-required precondition such as If-Match is absent.
429 with Retry-After when known for rate-limited requests; never for validation failures.
500 for unexpected internal failures via centralized handling and ProblemDetails.
502 only when acting as an intermediary that received an invalid upstream response; not every dependency failure.
503 with Retry-After when meaningful for temporary inability to serve.
504 only when acting as an intermediary whose upstream did not respond in time.
When a repeated POST must not duplicate effects consider an Idempotency-Key; reusing a key with a materially different payload returns 409.
Use standard conditional-request semantics (ETag, If-Match, 412, 428) instead of custom status codes.
Configure stable headers on the client; apply per-request values such as dynamic tokens per request or through a handler; never mutate shared DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently.
Prefer System.Net.Http.Json/System.Text.Json with explicit options when the remote contract differs; do not reuse Domain entities as remote contracts.
Hedging only for operations safe to execute several times; never hedge state-changing operations.
Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; prefer the provider's execution strategy.

Prefer platform trace identifiers; add an explicit correlation identifier only for an integration or operational requirement; validate or normalize externally accepted identifiers; propagate tracing context across outbound calls.
Normal structured logging is sufficient for most code; use source-generated logging for a measured high-volume path.
Use var when the type is obvious or unimportant; keep implementation details non-public; sealed only when deliberately not designed for inheritance.
Standard .NET naming: PascalCase for types and public members, camelCase for parameters and locals, meaningful names.
Prefer immutability when it represents the model naturally; do not force it where controlled mutation is simpler.
Span<T>, stackalloc, pooling and similar are performance tools: ordinary collections by default, introduced only when profiling or a clear hot path justifies them.
Add only the references layout.md maps, as ProjectReference items written into the project files (not through reference commands).
Include the hook's reference-change and outward-reference reports in the scaffolding report.
Every security report states the static-analysis limitation.
Severity uses the five levels Critical (sparingly), High, Medium, Low, Info.
Each confirmed finding gives severity, file and location, title, evidence, why it is a risk, likely impact, smallest remediation and OWASP category when applicable.
The report contains scope, limitations, a severity summary, findings and per-layer results.
Security review reports concrete risks in the context of actual exposure.
Distinguish confirmed findings from items needing verification and assign severity from exploitability, reachability, impact and context, never mechanically from a pattern, CVSS or OWASP category.
Do not suppress a real secret because it sits in a Development file.
Name workflows needing threat modeling instead of claiming the scan proves them secure.
Never invent exploitability.
Normalize user-controlled paths and verify they stay within the intended storage boundary (traversal, absolute-path injection, archive extraction).
Never deserialize untrusted payloads into arbitrary runtime types (BinaryFormatter, unsafe TypeNameHandling).
template-maintenance runs only when the user invokes it (disable-model-invocation; never started automatically).
Maintenance keeps the always-loaded surface compact (CLAUDE.md plus the two imported decision summaries; the checker prints its estimate).
Place each statement at the level of the most volatile thing it depends on (Level 3 project, Level 2 technology, Level 1 architecture, else Level 0) and split mixed statements.
State each rule once in its owner; elsewhere use only routing pointers or short check-by-reference items.

Every artifact starts with the one-line header and every rule file declares paths; Depends on points only to the same or a more stable level; Levels 0 and 1 name no concrete technologies; update the instruction map for every added, moved or removed artifact.
Verification starts by reviewing the final changed-file set and diff: scope (no accidental unrelated refactoring), no generated/build artifacts, secrets or environment-specific credentials.
Temporary diagnostics are removed only after their uniquely verified behavior is preserved.
Determine the affected areas before choosing checks.
After fixes review the final diff again for unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, TODO/FIXME, stale temporary tests and architecture drift.
The final diff has no unapproved drift from product inputs and no stale surfaces after a settings change.
Build the affected backend solution/projects and the frontend with its configured script.
A build failure means the implementation is not complete.
Run relevant tests (the whole suite for small solutions, affected projects first for large ones).
Investigate every newly failing relevant test.
The checker hardcodes four level directories and names, the instruction-map path and a 5500-token always-loaded budget.
The checker requires the listed workflow and knowledge skills and forbids standalone serilog/resilience skills.
Every artifact needs the exact classification header with matching level names; no 'Kind:' classification.
Rule files live in .claude/rules/{0-core,1-architecture,2-technology,3-project}/ with a matching header level and a non-empty paths list.
CLAUDE.md must be Level 0, its imports must resolve and it must import overview.md and decisions.md; additional imports raise a warning.
Level 0 and 1 instruction files must not name concrete technologies (lexical check over the text).
Conformance dependencies must not point to product inputs, must point only to the same or a more stable level and must be acyclic.
Internal references must resolve; skill-private references may be used only by their owning skill; named skills/agents, routed workflows and CLAUDE.md routing targets must exist.
Files named like manifests, contracts, slots or capabilities under .claude/ are errors.
The instruction map must list every instruction artifact, hook, tool and settings.json.
The always-loaded surface is estimated (characters/4) and warned above 5500 tokens.
File-scoped namespaces (suggestion), System usings first, usings outside the namespace, IDE0005 unused usings as warning.
var when the type is apparent; explicit types for built-in types and elsewhere (suggestion).
Modern syntax preferences are suggestions or silent only (no mechanical modernization).
Braces when multiline (suggestion); expression-bodied methods on single lines (silent).
PascalCase types and members, I-prefixed interfaces, camelCase parameters and locals (suggestion).
Async methods carry the Async suffix (suggestion).
Classify every consequential choice as Decided, Delegated or Reserved.
Decided choices (instruction system, product inputs, recorded decisions, incl. choices required by the specification or established structure) are followed and not reopened without approval.
Delegated choices (local, reversible, no change to a boundary, dependency, accepted convention, public contract or observable behavior) are decided without asking.
Reserved choices require explicit approval before implementation.
An explicit user instruction counts as approval.
If an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable product behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Defining product behavior or tunable values the product sources do not define is Reserved.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior do not require approval.
Do not ask approval for routine decisions already constrained by product sources, the approved stack, existing code or these rules.
Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior: propose it with the reason, ask for approval and record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Synchronize every affected surface of an approved tunable value (custom-settings).
Reserved decisions need explicit approval before implementation.
Changing an accepted project or architecture decision is Reserved.
Adopting a new architectural style or pattern (CQRS, mediator, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices, Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns) is Reserved.
Adding a production project, layer or assembly is Reserved.
Changing persistence boundaries (incl. multiple persistence contexts) or persistence technology is Reserved.
Adding a messaging, background processing or distributed cache infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a search, external storage or external identity infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a major library/framework is Reserved.
Replacing approved baseline technology is Reserved.
Introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction (e.g. a project-wide Result model) is Reserved.
Changing the authentication/authorization architecture is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
For a Reserved decision present a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) and run architecture-decision.
In an autonomous or headless run take only a policy-compliant non-Reserved path, never make a Reserved decision silently and list every unresolved Decision Request in the final report.
Nullable reference types, implicit usings and the latest analysis level are enabled repository-wide in Directory.Build.props.
EnforceCodeStyleInBuild with GenerateDocumentationFile (CS1591 suppressed) reports code-style diagnostics such as IDE0005 during build.

reviewer_text: SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, feature specifications and task prompts are inputs, not instruction layers; they may request a decision change but never silently override engineering policy (reported as not clearly distinguishing explicitly authorized deviations).

SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; on an apparent conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected (reported as excluding resolution from already clear requirements).

Decisions are classified Decided/Delegated/Reserved; the Reserved list includes changing the project reference graph, a fixed Decision Request procedure applies, and in an unclear case any 'yes' (including adding, removing or replacing a dependency or changing a reference boundary) makes it Reserved (reported tension with the Delegated class for internal dependency/reference changes).
Editor defaults: UTF-8, final newline, trimmed trailing whitespace (not for Markdown), space indentation of 4 by default and 2 for JSON/YAML/TS/HTML/SCSS/CSS/Markdown and MSBuild/XML files.

Async methods end with Async unless a framework or existing contract prevents it; the configured naming rule detects the async modifier and applies the suffix without that exception (reported divergence for Task-returning non-async methods and framework-named overrides).
.env and .env.* (except .env.example) and appsettings.*.local.json are git-ignored (reported as possibly excluding intentional non-secret configuration from review).
Directory.Build.props enables Nullable and ImplicitUsings for every .NET project (reported as unconditional).

Every NuGet package version lives in Directory.Packages.props; project files use versionless PackageReference entries; versions are added or updated only through add-dependency (latest stable compatible version verified at install time) (reported as an unconditional build switch).
The code-reviewer's read-only role is enforced by disallowing Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit; shell-based writes are not mechanically excluded.
The architecture check maps projects to roles by name pattern and forbids the ASP.NET Core shared framework in inner roles (reported approximation of semantic boundaries).
Supporting type roles are clear from name and/or directory using suffixes such as Service, Dto, Request/Response, Result/Outcome, Validator, Rules/Policy, Factory, Mapper, Adapter.
Program.cs calls the layer registration methods AddApplication() and AddInfrastructure(configuration).
Replace all four frame facets together, keep roles.md unchanged unless the role vocabulary itself changes (Reserved), and update the selection record.

Frame implementations express every role, keep leaf technology out of frame facets and declare non-role bindings; a frame replacement (Reserved, with ADR) supplies every facet and updates the selection record and the CLAUDE.md import.
The backend-testing slot requires framework rule, commands, enforcement and knowledge facets; replacing the framework replaces the whole module and is a Reserved selection change with an ADR.

Baseline test packages: NUnit, NUnit3TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, NUnit.Analyzers (template default), Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing for integration tests, Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing when time control is useful.
xunit, MSTest and TUnit packages are flagged as a second test framework (reported as requiring approval rather than only a concrete reason).
Confirm the installed Angular CLI's flags with ng new --help rather than from memory before creating the workspace.
Inspect package.json before running anything; use scripts that exist and never invent script names.
Frontend package prefixes (@ngrx/, @ngxs/, axios, lodash, bootstrap, @ng-bootstrap/, ngx-bootstrap, primeng, tailwindcss) are approval-required packages matched by prefix.
Removing the Angular module deletes every listed file and the module directory, removes the frontend-stack import from CLAUDE.md and sets the frontend selection row to none.
Clearing the optional frontend selection: set the selection row to none, delete manifest-listed files, remove the frontend-stack import and map rows, run the checker.
A missing required facet is a conformance failure: raise a Decision Request instead of shipping the module.
Remove a migration only when it is unapplied and uncommitted.
Database update/drop commands are for Development only and never point at Production; production migration is a deployment step.
Inner roles must not reference packages with the Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore prefix (prefix match).
Model co-change detection covers only backend/*.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/** paths (reported gap for differently located DbContext files).
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly, Polly.Extensions.Http, FluentValidation.AspNetCore and Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch are deny-listed packages that must not be added.
Use an injectable time abstraction for logic depending on the current clock that needs deterministic tests (marked default); do not mechanically replace stored or explicit timestamps.
Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access services; do not scatter HTTP calls; never import backend domain or persistence types into the frontend.
Return problem-details responses (RFC 9457) for non-validation HTTP failures and validation problem-details for request validation (marked default); keep machine-readable contracts stable and safe.
Log an unexpected exception once, at the boundary that handles it, not again in repository, use-case, entry-point and global handler.
Once external clients rely on an API version, avoid silent breaking changes; a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
Liveness avoids external dependencies whose outage could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on capabilities required to serve traffic and reflects startup and dependency availability.
The technology-neutral testing rule file loads only for backend test paths (reported: frontend test work depends on other routing).

Role-to-project mapping with fixed names and paths: backend/<Name>.Domain, .Application, .Infrastructure, .Api and test projects .Application.Tests and .IntegrationTests (optional .Domain.Tests, .Infrastructure.Tests).
Instructions outside the selected architecture frame use the role vocabulary instead of frame-specific layer names.
The backend-libraries rule file loads only for backend paths (reported: a repository-root Dockerfile edit may not load the container rules).
Controller classes live in a Controllers/ folder of the entry-point project.
The time abstraction is TimeProvider (TimeProvider.System injected; tests use FakeTimeProvider).
Local development secrets use dotnet user-secrets.
Current stable Angular is the latest release supported by the selected Node.js environment at scaffolding time (reported: this may allow an older Angular instead of upgrading Node).
Package versions live only in Directory.Packages.props; project PackageReference entries are versionless and never duplicate a central version.
The architecture check reports a violation whenever a top-level 'tests' path exists (file or directory).
Projects whose names match no frame role are only warned about and skipped in reference checks.
Inner-role checks match direct framework references, implying SDKs and package-name prefixes (reported overmatch of neutral APIs and blind spots for transitive or imported references).

The post-change hook recognizes only .csproj, Directory.Packages.props and package.json as manifests (reported: imported props/targets and npm configuration that change dependency behavior are missed).

MSBuild-property versions need manual confirmation, floating or empty versions are flagged for pinning and prereleases are allowed only when explicitly requested (no explicit-request exception for floating versions).
The post-change hook returns only architecture violations, not warnings.
Any change to SPECIFICATION.md or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md returns a reminder to keep them consistent and run the custom-settings workflow.
A denied dependency command passes when the identical command is retried within a fixed 30-minute grace window.
An identical retry of a denied dependency command passes without verifying that the add-dependency due diligence occurred (the gate is effectively a reminder).
Malformed or incomplete hook input or an internal failure blocks any shell command (fail closed).
The co-change Stop hook emits a blocking decision once per change state and requires each item to be handled or stated as not applicable.
The instruction map imposes four stability levels, technology-neutral vocabulary in Core/Architecture, one-line artifact headers and a checker run after every change.
The instruction checker's API-shape heuristics treat PascalCase/camelCase identifiers as technology names (reported: stricter than semantic technology neutrality).
Every artifact needs a header starting with '> Level: ' with a known Level and Owns and Loading fields; a 'Kind:' field is a failure.

The checker allows only the four agreed slot directories, requires a selected implementation for required slots and requires implementation directories to equal the selection (no stored alternatives).
A module's binds must be 'none' or '<frame> — <reason>' with a minimum reason length, and binds are required when module content uses frame-specific vocabulary or the contract requires them.
A rule may reference only same-or-more-stable artifacts; the only exempt reverse reference is a narrowly formatted 'Framework binding: `<slot>.<facet>`' pointer.

Hooks must use exec form (bare command, script argument under ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks, no expansion) with numeric timeouts; only PreToolUse sets onFailure block; PreToolUse, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure must cover the shell (and edit) tools and a Stop hook must exist.
The project parser reads .csproj XML without evaluating conditions or imports (reported accuracy limits for conditional references and imported central package settings).
Bash/PowerShell calls run the pre-shell hook through node with a 15-second timeout and onFailure block (fail closed).
Report package, version, license, vulnerability/deprecation result, target project and approvals obtained or still pending.
Create directories only when they hold meaningful code; a feature owns its UI and data access; move code to shared only when it genuinely crosses features.
State escalation path: component state, then signals, then a feature service/store, then RxJS composition, and a state library only when demonstrated complexity needs it.
Use Material components consistently for common primitives when they satisfy the requirement; do not wrap every Material component in a custom abstraction without a reason.
Adopting API versioning is Reserved; versioning belongs to the API contract and the package is added only after adoption.
The error-handling example maps request cancellation to status 499 (reported as a status choice beyond the cancellation rule).

FluentValidation fits required input, constraints, ranges and conditional rules; validators are registered with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions; follow the established invocation pattern and do not add deprecated automatic-validation integrations.

Catch only to recover, translate, perform a defined fallback, add context preserving the original, or run required cleanup; never swallow exceptions; catch/log/rethrow is redundant when the global handler logs.
If a Result pattern is adopted use typed errors, never arbitrary string arrays.
Keep repeated policy names in constants; use roles when the business model is genuinely role-oriented; prefer a policy when several roles or claims form one capability.
Use-case code never depends on HttpContext, ClaimsPrincipal or IHttpContextAccessor; repeated caller-identity needs use a small use-case abstraction implemented at an outer boundary.

Check the toolchain (dotnet --info/--version, node --version, package manager, global.json, target frameworks, CI runtimes); never change declared SDK/Node/framework versions because the local machine differs; report an unavailable toolchain.

Use several focused attempts, not an unlimited loop; stop and reassess when the same root failure survives different fixes, fixes create unrelated failures, or toolchain, infrastructure or package problems block progress.
Cache keys include entity id, tenant, user when genuinely user-specific, locale and relevant query parameters; centralize key construction once formats repeat.
Use the CI platform's secret or identity mechanism, preferring workload/federated identity over long-lived credentials; CI and CD may be separate with environment protection and approvals.
Read the rule files whose paths match the changed files (a separate review context may not have them loaded) and the knowledge skill for each specialized area touched.
Check role/frame boundary and persistence-access rules and run check-architecture.mjs when project references or packages changed.

Severity scale: Critical (data loss, security vulnerability, reliably broken core behavior; blocks use or merge), High (fix before merge), Medium (real maintainability, robustness or test gap), Low (non-blocking improvement).
appsettings.json holds structure and non-secret defaults only; Development values come from dotnet user-secrets; deployed environments use platform injection or the chosen managed store.
Configuration anti-patterns: services reading string keys from IConfiguration, secrets in committed settings files, Configure<T>(section) without validation for settings the app cannot run without.
Record an approved setting under a stable descriptive name with value and purpose, then update the owning code, validation, configuration and tests.
Never apply production database migrations automatically from normal application startup; production migration is an explicit deployment operation using approved credentials.
Copy project files explicitly before the source tree so source edits do not invalidate the restore layer; update this when the structure changes; avoid flattening wildcard tricks.
Verify container changes: build the image, verify startup, port and configuration, non-root behavior when relevant, health-probe integration and that no secrets or stray files landed in the image.
Prefer one observable scenario per test; a multi-step test fits when the sequence is the scenario.
Host integration tests configure the Testing environment with isolated resources so they never reach a Development or Production database, exposing Program to the factory where needed.
External services use fakes, stub handlers or local fake servers (a sandbox only when explicitly targeted); slow or unreliable external tests stay out of the fast run.
Use interceptors for infrastructure cross-cutting behavior such as auditing; never hide business behavior in them.
Fresh local seed data comes from explicitly recreating the local database; test data uses dedicated test setup, never the seeder.
Run verify before preparing a PR (reported as required even when valid checks already completed or when only drafting a description).
Keep readiness unhealthy until required asynchronous startup work completes; liveness never represents that startup state.
For HTTP-level optimistic concurrency use standard conditional requests (ETag on GET; If-Match on PUT/PATCH; changed gives 412) rather than custom status codes.
Prefer System.Net.Http.Json/System.Text.Json with explicit options when the remote contract differs; do not reuse domain entities as remote contracts.
The Serilog bootstrap example logs a fatal startup failure without rethrowing or setting a failure exit status (reported failure-visibility uncertainty).
The C# property example trims and rejects blank names silently (reported copy risk for unapproved string semantics).

Every security report states that the static review is not a penetration test and cannot prove the application secure (it may miss runtime-only, infrastructure, business-logic, authorization-bypass, deployment-specific and dynamic-exploitation issues).
Small solutions run the full test suite; large solutions run affected projects first, then the broader suite the risk requires.

Report what was actually run per area (backend build, frontend build, tests, runtime smoke, architecture check, formatting, security/dependency scan, diff review) using NOT RUN or NOT APPLICABLE rather than implying that an unchecked area passed.
Every instruction artifact is placed by stability (0-core, 1-architecture, 2-technology, 3-project).
Every artifact starts with a one-line header (Level, optional Capability/Facet, Owns, Scope, Loading).
Conformance dependencies point only to the same or a more stable level.

Core and Architecture name no concrete implementation technology in any form, pointers included, except the fixed vocabulary (.NET, C#, TypeScript, Git, HTTP; ASP.NET Core and NuGet not exempt), and refer to Level 2 only by role, capability, facet or a technology-neutral skill name.

When SPECIFICATION.md or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md is edited, keep the two consistent and run custom-settings (PostToolUse feedback).
At Stop, a changed product source is reminded once per change state.
Changing the project reference graph is Reserved unless it implements the approved layout; every dotnet add/remove reference and dotnet reference add/remove command requires user confirmation.
