Peer-dependency bypass flags trigger an 'ask' decision; the command runs only if the user confirms.
Every project-reference command triggers an 'ask' decision (Reserved unless it implements the approved layout), even when it implements that layout.
Use in-process host integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication, DI, repositories, the ORM or persistence is what the test must prove (marked default).

Use the actual database provider when relational or provider behavior matters (an isolated real-provider container is optional); never claim provider fidelity from a different provider (marked default).
The backend follows Clean Architecture.

Role-to-project mapping: domain model = backend/<Name>.Domain; use-case layer with Application Services, persistence-access contracts and IUnitOfWork = <Name>.Application; implementation layer = <Name>.Infrastructure; entry point and composition root (Program.cs) = <Name>.Api; test projects <Name>.Application.Tests and <Name>.IntegrationTests (optional Domain.Tests, Infrastructure.Tests).
Do not introduce CQRS command/query handlers, mediator libraries or mediator-based request dispatch, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar unless explicitly approved.
A service growing too large is a signal to reconsider its responsibilities, not a reason to adopt another pattern.
Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic repository base may exist only inside Infrastructure to remove real duplication.
Repositories in one use case share the scoped Unit of Work and persistence context; inject repositories explicitly; IUnitOfWork must not become a repository container or service locator.
IUnitOfWork (defined in Application) is the normal commit boundary of a use case; repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit.
The IUnitOfWork implementation delegates to AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync and staged changes are the shared context's tracked changes.
The entry-point mechanism is ASP.NET Core Controllers; do not create Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
Controller classes live in a Controllers/ folder of the entry-point project.
NUnit is the default .NET test framework; in an established project that deliberately uses another framework follow that convention; no second test framework without a concrete reason.
xunit, MSTest and TUnit packages are reported as requiring approval and to be removed unless approved (the hook escalates 'concrete reason' to approval).
An explicit case is an NUnit [TestCase] row; TestCaseSource counts as generated case machinery.
The integration-test host is WebApplicationFactory<Program>, created in [OneTimeSetUp] and disposed in [OneTimeTearDown].
For an empty Development database maintain a small deterministic representative seed dataset; no exhaustive combinations or random bulk data.
Keep substantial seed construction in a dedicated internal DbSeeder exposed through a narrow initialization extension.
When representative data exists (checked through anchor entities) leave it unchanged; the seeder never synchronizes, repairs, upgrades, overwrites or recreates; developers recreate explicitly.
Backend platform: .NET 10 LTS (latest stable servicing release), C# 14, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET Core Controllers; a preview/RC move requires approval.
Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the Development documentation and manual-testing surface at /swagger; exposure outside Development only when deployment requirements justify it.
Manual mapping for simple cases; Mapster (+ Mapster.DependencyInjection) is the approved mapping library when mapping volume warrants it.
Another mapping framework (AutoMapper) is a Reserved library addition reported as requiring approval.
Static composition: each required slot has exactly one selected implementation, the optional slot zero or one; only selected modules ship.
The default string comparison is the database default collation; relying on it for observable behavior requires approval.

The required workflow skills, shared knowledge skills and each selected module's knowledge skill exist; frontmatter name equals the directory with a description; template-maintenance is user-only and every other skill model-invocable.
Named skill/agent references and .claude path references resolve.
Skill-private references are used only by their owning skill.
Skill frontmatter names match directories with descriptions; template-maintenance is user-only and other skills stay model-invocable.
The code-reviewer agent must exist and disallow Write and Edit.
Skill-private references may be used only by their owning skill (the map may list them).
The instruction map must list every artifact and must not be imported by CLAUDE.md.
Mapping uses Mapster with Mapster.DependencyInjection.
Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience / Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience are the resilience packages when resilience is required; the deprecated Polly integrations are never added.
Before installing check whether the exact package/version is deprecated.
Check known vulnerability information (dotnet package list --vulnerable --include-transitive, the frontend audit command).
Verify the exact selected version's license from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary).
Permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) are acceptable without approval; being free to download does not make a package acceptable.

Do not install automatically when a package requires payment or a commercial license, or its license has material obligations or cannot be confidently classified; present the concern and reasonable alternatives (say so when none exists) and never substitute silently.
Make no legal conclusions beyond published license information.
Use computed for derived state and avoid effect() when computed, template binding or explicit event handling is clearer.
Manual subscriptions in components and services use takeUntilDestroyed() or DestroyRef to tie their lifetime to the owner.

Every approved Reserved decision is recorded as an ADR at docs/decisions/NNNN-<kebab-title>.md (Status Accepted with date, Approved by, Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered), docs/decisions/ being created with the first ADR.
The decision is summarized in the decision file of the owning level (frame style rule, decisions.md, frontend stack rule), never in a single cross-level register.
The summary is a decision line pointing to the ADR, without restating rules that live elsewhere.
Record an approved Reserved decision as a numbered ADR at docs/decisions/NNNN-<kebab-title>.md with Status/Approved by, Context, Decision, Consequences and Alternatives considered.
Update the decision file at the level the decision belongs to, never a single cross-level register.
Record the change as a decision summary line pointing to the ADR without restating rules that live elsewhere.
Changing a slot implementation (or clearing the optional frontend) always needs an ADR.
A changed declared property that affects observable behavior (e.g. string comparison) also needs product approval.

Choose the authentication scheme by application type: Bearer/OIDC for a browser SPA calling an API, cookies for server-rendered apps, Identity for owned local accounts, an external OIDC/OAuth provider when identity is delegated.
Do not issue custom JWTs when an existing provider already issues tokens.
Build-fix starts by reproducing the actual failure with the narrowest reliable command.
Read the complete output, group errors by root cause and fix root causes before downstream symptoms.
When tests fail decide whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentional contract change is at fault.
Determine the authoritative contract instead of patching both sides of a cross-stack break into inconsistent shapes.
Never fabricate replacement APIs.
Repair in small bounded iterations: after each meaningful fix rerun the narrowest failing check and widen only after the focused failure is resolved.
Do not run unrelated build systems.
Use several focused attempts rather than an unlimited loop and never repeat variants of a failed guess.
Stop and reassess when progress stalls.

Repairs never bypass architecture: no invalid or outward project references to make a type compile, persistence types in the use-case layer, business logic in entry points, client-only authorization or scattered HTTP calls.
Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing.
When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine user input is required.
Never claim a problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains.
Never leave the repository knowingly worse; unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.
When a required toolchain is unavailable report the limitation instead of editing source or changing declared SDK/runtime versions.
CI definitions stay in source control and reproduce the repository's supported build/test commands for the parts that actually exist (no assumed providers, containers or tooling).
No optional formatter turned into a gate without adoption.
CI restores from a clean environment without developer-machine state and keeps build/test failures visible.
Review reports concrete defects or risks.

Findings are prioritized as correctness; security and authorization; data integrity and persistence; architectural boundary violations; concurrency and integration; missing meaningful tests; maintainability; evidence-supported performance; style preferences are never ranked above behavioral defects.
The reviewer does not rewrite working code, report tooling-owned formatting, demand personal style or unadopted patterns, recommend speculative optimizations, or add filler praise.
Do not invent failures without a plausible execution path.
Do not manufacture findings to populate categories; when there are no meaningful findings say so and name important areas that could not be verified.
Code-review output gives for each finding severity, file/location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix, ordered by severity.

Severity scale: Critical (data loss, security vulnerability, reliably broken core behavior; blocks merge), High (likely defect or architecture/data-integrity issue; fix before merge), Medium (real maintainability, robustness or test gap), Low (non-blocking improvement).

When an approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value is added, changed or removed, identify and update every affected surface (owning code, validators and request constraints, domain/use-case checks, database mapping, frontend validation and hints, tests and test data, documentation, mirrored configuration); a single changed literal does not establish synchronization.
Search for stale references and run the normal verification.
Keep frontend validation synchronized while the backend stays authoritative.
Change only affected behavior.
Lifetimes: use-case units using repositories/commit boundary scoped; stateless helpers transient or concrete; immutable configuration singleton-compatible; persistence context scoped.
A singleton or hosted service that needs scoped work creates a scope per operation and resolves a scoped orchestration service, not implementation internals.
Decorators via Scrutor only when it is already present; Scrutor is not added for one decoration.
Convention scanning only when registration volume creates real boilerplate; scan the assembly that owns the services.
The development-workflow output summarizes what changed, Delegated decisions taken and the verify report.
The output lists open (Reserved) Decision Requests.
Keep entity configuration in IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> classes.
Keep persistence-specific configuration out of domain-model entities where practical.
Tracking queries for entities that will be modified and committed; AsNoTracking() for read-only entity queries; not needed on projections.
Avoid lazy loading by default (hidden queries, N+1).
Raw SQL only when LINQ cannot express the query effectively or measurement justifies it.
Start with clear LINQ; before optimizing inspect round trips, selected columns, N+1, indexes, generated SQL, plans, materialized volume and tracking.
Place the Development seeder under Persistence/Seeding/ in the implementation project.
When the required seed graph is complex, ask for the desired dataset instead of inventing a large generic one.
Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean, stash away or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.
Never remove a worktree holding uncommitted user work.
Never stash, reset or discard automatically to let a merge or rebase proceed.

Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (status, diffs, current branch, upstream) and use the minimum operation that achieves the request; never silently clean unrelated working-tree changes.
Before a high-risk operation inspect what it would lose or rewrite.
Never stashing away user work is stated categorically (reported as restricting even an explicitly requested, recoverable stash).
Protected/shared branches are treated as non-rewritable, stated alongside the explicit-request/approved-workflow allowance for rebasing shared history and force pushes (reported tension).
Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the requested logical change; never stage unrelated modified files.
One logical change per commit with implementation and its tests together; no unrelated fixes bundled.
Avoid pushing unrelated local commits.
Prefer one logical change per commit; implementation and its protecting tests normally together; no artificial micro-commits; no unrelated fixes bundled.
Follow the repository's commit-message convention; otherwise Conventional Commits are a useful default.
For 201 Created include Location when a stable URI exists.
For 202 Accepted return an operation id or a Location where progress is observable.
Choose one convention for repeated DELETE of an absent resource (204 or 404) and apply it consistently across equivalent resources.
406 when no acceptable representation can be produced; 415 for unsupported request media types.
422 for structurally valid requests with invalid semantics or business input.
428 when the contract requires a precondition the client omitted (missing If-Match gives 428; stale If-Match gives 412).
429 for rate-limited requests, with Retry-After when known; never for validation failures.
Retry only plausibly transient failures; never retry validation failures, authentication/authorization failures, permanent 404s or deterministic business rejections.
Do not wrap normal ORM operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; prefer the provider's own execution strategy; HTTP retry policies are not database policies.
Prefer platform trace identifiers; add an explicit correlation id only for a concrete integration or operational need; propagate tracing context across outbound calls.
Validate or normalize correlation ids accepted from clients.
Prefer destructuring to selected properties and keep destructuring limits configured.
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch is deprecated; use Elastic.Serilog.Sinks when Elasticsearch is the chosen log store.

Span/ReadOnlySpan, stack allocation, ArrayPool/MemoryPool pooling, preallocated buffers and source-generated serialization are performance tools for demonstrated allocation-heavy hot paths, verified to help; ordinary arrays, strings and collections are the default.
Changing LangVersion or the target framework requires approval.
Reserved decisions need explicit approval.
Changing an accepted project/architecture decision is Reserved.

Adopting a new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS, mediator-based organization, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, a project-wide Result model, microservices) is Reserved.
Adding a production project/layer is Reserved.
Changing persistence boundaries (e.g. several persistence contexts) or persistence technology is Reserved.
Adding a messaging, background processing or distributed cache infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a search, external storage or external identity infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a major library/framework is Reserved.
Replacing approved baseline technology is Reserved.
Introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction is Reserved.
Changing the authentication/authorization architecture is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
The project-graph hook asks for confirmation of every reference command; confirm only references the approved layout shows.

Verify scaffolding: restore, build the solution, build the frontend when present, run tests when present, inspect project references with check-architecture.mjs, inspect the final tree, confirm Development configuration works, then run verify.
The entry-point project carries appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json.
Configure the launch profile so a Development run can open /swagger directly when that helps, keeping HTTP/HTTPS URLs consistent with the profile.
Frontend unit/component tests stay inside the frontend workspace (colocated); E2E under e2e/ when used.

global.json pins the intended SDK line: the current stable SDK of the target .NET release (no RC/preview unless explicitly requested) with a rollForward policy that allows normal patch/feature-band servicing.
Every security-scan report states the static-analysis limitation.
Reports use the five-level severity scale Critical (sparingly) / High / Medium / Low / Info.
Each confirmed finding gives severity, file and location, title, evidence, why it is a risk, likely impact, smallest remediation and OWASP category when applicable.
The report contains scope, limitations, a severity summary table, findings and per-layer results.
Security review reports concrete risks in the context of actual exposure.
Security review distinguishes confirmed findings from items needing verification (NEEDS VERIFICATION).
Severity is assigned from exploitability, reachability, impact and application context, never from a suspicious pattern, an OWASP category or raw CVSS alone.
A real secret is not suppressed because it sits in a Development file.
Workflows needing threat modeling are named instead of claiming the scan proves them secure.
Never invent exploitability the code does not establish.
Each confirmed finding gives severity, file and location, title, evidence, why it is a risk, likely impact, smallest remediation and OWASP category when applicable.
The report follows the template: Scope, Limitations, severity Summary table, Findings and Layer Results.
Layer status is PASS, FINDINGS, NOT APPLICABLE or NOT CHECKED.
Never PASS for an uninspected layer.
Normalize and verify that user-controlled paths stay inside the intended root (reported as possibly an illustrative review prompt rather than a mandatory rule).
Review for unsafe deserialization: BinaryFormatter, unsafe TypeNameHandling, deserializing untrusted payloads into arbitrary runtime types (reported as possibly illustrative).
When the contract feeds client generation, avoid anonymous response shapes and use explicit request/response contracts.
After API behavior changes open the Development Swagger UI and exercise representative endpoints (reported as required for every API behavior change).

Place content by kind: normative constraint to a rule; multi-step procedure to a workflow skill; technique/examples to a knowledge skill or private reference; product facts to SPECIFICATION.md/CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md; mechanical check to a hook, script or configuration.

Place content by level, first match wins: project-specific selection/layout/default to 3-project; concrete non-platform technology to 2-technology; adopted architecture/role/boundary to 1-architecture; otherwise 0-core.
Content specific to a selected slot implementation goes into that module's facets and declares Capability; everything else uses roles and <slot>.<facet> references, never implementation names.
Always-needed planning policy goes into CLAUDE.md or an imported always rule; path-specific policy into a rule whose paths cover its scope; procedure obligations into the owning workflow.
Add each rule once; elsewhere use a pointer or a yes/no check naming the owner.
Keep the header line (Level, Capability when module-owned, Owns, Scope, Loading).
Update INSTRUCTION_MAP.md (level tables, capability view, policy locator).
Run check-instructions.mjs and fix every reported item.
Always-needed planning policy goes into CLAUDE.md or an imported always rule; path-specific policy into a rule whose paths cover at least its scope; procedure obligations into the owning workflow.
Each rule has one owner; elsewhere only a pointer or a yes/no check naming the owner.
The always-loaded surface (CLAUDE.md, its imports, skill descriptions) stays compact: path or workflow policy is not moved into it and always-needed policy is not moved out of it to save tokens.

Verification starts by reviewing the final changed-file set and diff: confirm scope (no unrelated refactoring), no accidental generated/build artifacts, no secrets or environment-specific credentials.
Remove temporary diagnostics only after their uniquely verified behavior is preserved.
After fixes review the final diff again (unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, stale temporary tests, architecture or specification drift, stale settings surfaces).
Determine the affected areas before choosing checks.

When the change touches architectural boundaries (project references, entry point to use-case flow, persistence-access contracts, persistence confinement, commit boundary, dependency direction) check the boundary rules under 1-architecture and run check-architecture.mjs.
For dependency changes or security-sensitive work run dotnet package list --vulnerable --include-transitive (when the SDK supports it) and the frontend audit command.
System directives first, no separated import groups, using directives outside the namespace (suggestions).
var when the type is apparent; explicit types for built-in types (suggestions).
Prefer braces (suggestion).
If an omitted detail must be decided and it materially affects observable behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Defining product behavior or tunable values not defined by product sources is Reserved.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior do not require approval.
Delegated decisions (local, reversible, no material change to a boundary, dependency, accepted convention, public contract or observable behavior) are decided without asking.
Do not ask approval for routine choices already constrained by the specification, approved stack, existing code or rules.
Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior: propose it with a reason, get approval and record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
After recording, synchronize affected surfaces (custom-settings).
Classify decisions as Decided, Delegated or Reserved.
Decided choices (settled by imported decision files, approved product sources or recorded decisions) are followed; reopening requires approval.
Reserved decisions require approval.
An explicit user instruction counts as approval.
Changing accepted decisions is Reserved.
Adopting new architectural styles/patterns (Rich Domain/DDD, CQRS, mediator, VSA, event sourcing, project-wide Result, microservices) is Reserved.
Adding new production projects/layers is Reserved.
Persistence boundary or technology changes are Reserved.
Adding messaging, background processing or distributed cache infrastructure is Reserved.
Replacing baseline technology is Reserved.
Changing the authentication architecture is Reserved.

Changing a capability selection (changing the architecture frame, replacing a leaf implementation, changing the database provider inside persistence, clearing the optional frontend) is Reserved and needs explicit approval through a Decision Request.
Replacing approved baseline technology is Reserved and needs explicit approval through a Decision Request.
For a Reserved decision send a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) and continue only with non-Reserved work.
Do not ask approval for routine choices already constrained by the specification, approved stack, existing code or rules.
Any implementation work (feature, bug fix, refactor, performance, CI/CD or deployment change) runs development-workflow; work is not complete until its verify step has run.

Specialized work goes to the named workflow: dependency add/update/remove to add-dependency, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes to custom-settings, solution/project structure to project-structure, accepted Reserved decisions to architecture-decision, failing build/tests to build-fix, review to code-review, security audit to security-scan, Git operations to git-workflow.

reviewer_text: New applications install the packages each decision names plus scaffold packages: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design where migrations are created, a Console sink for local logging, NUnit3TestAdapter and Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk in test projects (reported as fixed packages beyond the concrete-need rule).

The local connection-string example trusts the server certificate, while the prose forbids committing any usernames, passwords, tokens, production hosts or production connection strings (reported: broader than real secret credentials).

A project-reference change outside the accepted graph is Reserved: raise a Decision Request and, after approval, run the reference command with the trailing comment '# project-references: approved' (reported: even legal internal references need a literal approval marker).
Every security report states that the scan is an evidence-based static review, not a penetration test, and cannot prove the application secure (reported as required even for a narrow verified issue).
No generated or build artifacts were added to the change (reported as barring intentionally maintained generated source, broader than removing accidental artifacts).
Small solutions run the complete test suite; large solutions run affected test projects first, then the broader suite the risk requires (reported as regardless of scope and risk).
Report what was actually run with PASS, FAIL, NOT RUN or NOT APPLICABLE; the example matrix omits FAIL/NOT RUN for some areas (reported risk of incomplete skipped-check reports).
Application services, repositories and external adapters use interface-to-implementation registration at architectural boundaries; implementation-only helpers can be registered concretely.
Load the knowledge skill for each technology involved (reported as required regardless of relevance).

The development-workflow output states what changed and why, Delegated decisions taken, Decision Requests raised or still unresolved, and the verification report (reported as requiring enumeration of Delegated decisions).
Keep build tooling out of production runtime images (reported as broader than avoiding SDK images for convenience).
Configure the Testing environment with isolated test resources so an integration test cannot reach a development or production database by accident (reported: the environment name is prescribed).
Keep slow or unreliable external-system tests separate from ordinary fast runs (reported as regardless of existing suite design).
Keep entity configuration in IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> classes (reported as prescribed beyond confining persistence configuration to Infrastructure).
Paginate in the database with deterministic ordering; the example orders only by CreatedAt (reported: equal timestamps are not uniquely ordered).

Detect existing data with representative root/anchor entities; the seeder assumes the schema is already migrated; for a new local database apply migrations first, then startup seeds the empty schema (reported: the detection method and startup trigger are prescribed).
Raw SQL fits queries EF Core cannot express effectively or a measured performance need (reported as narrower than a measured or clearly demonstrated need).

Additional status mappings: 406/415 for negotiation and media types, 409, 412, 422, 428, 429 with Retry-After when known, 500, 502, 503 with Retry-After when meaningful, and 504, each with stated limits.
When HTTP optimistic concurrency is part of the contract use standard conditional requests (ETag/If-Match) instead of custom status codes.
The Microsoft resilience packages build on Polly v8, but application code uses the Microsoft.Extensions resilience APIs (reported as omitting the direct-Polly exception).
The Serilog bootstrap example logs a fatal startup failure without rethrowing or setting a failure exit code (reported failure-visibility uncertainty).
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch is deprecated; use Elastic.Serilog.Sinks (reported: a fixed replacement and log-storage defaults may be acted on beyond version-specific due diligence).
The C# property example trims and rejects blank names silently (reported copy risk for unapproved string semantics).
Api Controllers are thin ASP.NET Core Controllers; no Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested (reported as stricter than Controllers merely being the default).

The add-dependency output reports package, selected version and why, license, deprecation and vulnerability status, approval obtained, files changed and the verification result (reported as a fixed field set).
Use computed for derived state and avoid effect() when computed, template binding or explicit event handling expresses the dependency more clearly.
The error-handling example maps request cancellation to status 499 (reported as a status choice beyond the cancellation rule).

Stop and reassess when the same root failure survives different fixes, fixes create growing failures, toolchain or infrastructure is unavailable, compatibility cannot be resolved safely or correct behavior cannot be determined (reported: may halt independent source repair that is still possible).
Measure before adding caching purely for performance (reported as requiring measurement where a measured or reasoned need suffices).
The output-cache example embeds a five-minute TTL without a local illustrative-value caveat (reported copy risk).

Identify the changed behavior, error cases, effects and tests; read the standards for touched scopes and load the knowledge skill for each changed technology area (reported as required regardless of sufficient context).

Severity definitions: Critical (data loss, security vulnerability, reliably broken core behavior; blocks use or merge immediately), High (likely defect or architecture/data-integrity issue; fix before merge), Medium (real maintainability, robustness or test gap), Low (non-blocking improvement).

Product inputs may request a decision change but never silently override CLAUDE.md, the register or a standard; a deviation from a default needs a concrete reason and must be reported (reported: may constrain otherwise authorized specification choices).
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict; on conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected (reported as excluding resolution of an obviously stale source).

Decisions are classified Decided/Delegated/Reserved; the unclear-case test reserves any dependency addition/removal and any convention or reference change, and accepted decisions follow fixed reporting and recording procedures (reported tension with Delegated local changes).
Instruction-system changes go through /template-maintenance, which the user invokes (reported: required even when the user requests the change in ordinary language).
Editor defaults: UTF-8, final newline, trimmed trailing whitespace (not Markdown), 4-space indentation, 2 for JSON/YAML/TS/HTML/SCSS/CSS/project/XML/config files.

The naming rule suggests the Async suffix for methods with the async modifier (not by Task/ValueTask return type) and has no framework-contract exception (reported divergence from the coding standard).
Shared build configuration enables Nullable, ImplicitUsings and AnalysisLevel latest for every .NET project (reported as imposed regardless of project needs).

A security scan is an evidence-based static review, not a penetration test; state its limitations in the report.
Name security-sensitive workflows as threat-modeling or manual-review candidates instead of claiming the scan proves them secure.
Report concrete security risks, not generic advice.
Evaluate findings against actual exposure and application behavior, not mechanical pattern matches.
Never invent exploitability the code does not establish.
Label uncertain findings NEEDS VERIFICATION instead of presenting them as confirmed.
Never invent exploitability the code does not establish.
Confirmed findings are separated from NEEDS VERIFICATION items.
Security severity comes from exploitability, reachability, exposure, impact and context, never from a suspicious pattern, raw CVSS score or OWASP category alone.

Findings carry severity, location, title, evidence, risk, impact, remediation and OWASP category when applicable.
Distinguish confirmed findings from items needing verification.
Assign severity from exploitability, reachability, impact and context, never from a suspicious pattern or raw CVSS alone.
Recommend the smallest secure change consistent with the architecture.

Recommend the smallest secure change consistent with the architecture.

The review does not depend on a specific MCP server, agent, analyzer, commercial scanner or other external tool; tooling is evidence, not the sole authority.

Inspect which surfaces exist and skip irrelevant checks instead of reporting them as failures.

Layer status is PASS, FINDINGS, NOT APPLICABLE or NOT CHECKED; never PASS for an uninspected layer.

reviewer_text: Any API behavior change calls for opening the Development Swagger UI, alongside metadata/integration checks and conditional startup/endpoint exercises.
Instruction-system maintenance is user-invoked only and requires an explicit request to change that system.
Editor configuration sets UTF-8, spaces with a four-space default and two-space overrides for listed languages, final newlines and trailing-space trimming except Markdown.
Every Default deviation requires a concrete reason and reporting; must violations are defects and prefer/avoid are only guidance.
The complete named workflow routing table is mandatory rather than improvised; path standards load on reads and knowledge loads on demand.
Changing any decision-register entry is Reserved (reported: broader than only consequential technology or architecture replacements).
The declared SQL Server collation property characterizes defaults as case-insensitive while observable semantics stay a product decision; the actual deployment default remains unverified.
The documentation default expressly excludes built-in AddOpenApi/MapOpenApi as the baseline interactive surface.

The illustrative field-keyword setter trims and rejects whitespace without an explicit local approval caveat (reported: copying it into observable input handling would add unapproved normalization and validation).
The local connection-string example includes TrustServerCertificate=True despite the general certificate-validation prohibition; a local-scope exception is not explicitly resolved.
Scaffolding explicitly reads the named standards before files exist and loads private references selectively by the listed triggers.
Ordinary services consume typed options instead of configuration keys and parsing (reported: stronger than a general preference against scattered IConfiguration use).
Abstractions are used at Application-service as well as repository/external boundaries; concrete registration is allowed for implementation helpers.
EF configuration is placed in separate IEntityTypeConfiguration classes rather than only behind an Infrastructure boundary.
When no reasonable free alternative exists say so, and draw no legal conclusions beyond the published license.

Angular guidance: investigate sanitization bypasses, match server XSRF validation, specific behavioral test targets and a small default E2E suite; NgModules must not work around standalone setup failures.

URL-segment versioning is the default; header/query versioning when requirements justify it; strategies are not mixed without a concrete reason (reported: allows mixing that 'one strategy consistently' excludes).

Versioning knowledge adds same-Application-result mapping, client-generation compatibility considerations, version-grouped documents when needed and coexistence test topics without identical duplicated tests.
Capability changes require contract mapping, full old-facet removal, fixed paths and a green structure check; provider variants require synchronized manifest, register, facets and provider tests.
Unexpected exceptions propagate to one centralized handler; the example maps client-aborted requests to HTTP 499 (reported: the example's normativity is uncertain).
Typed outcomes are named by Application/business semantics (Validation, NotFound, Conflict, BusinessRuleViolation), not HTTP names (reported: NotFound/Conflict blur the HTTP-name boundary).
Authorization tests cover denied, unauthenticated, allowed, ownership and intended anonymous behavior rather than checking attributes alone.
Repair requires reading the complete relevant output, understanding a diagnostic before changing how it is reported, stopping when progress stalls and avoiding unrelated builds.

Repairs prohibit any/strict-mode shortcuts, independently patching mismatched contracts, reflexive lockfile deletion and changing declared toolchains to suit the local machine; upgrade replacements require verified documentation.
The manifest checker parses project files textually (Include references, raw attributes) without evaluating MSBuild conditions, properties or imports (reported uncertainty).
npm floating-version detection covers only empty, *, x, latest and next; ranges and other tags pass, while listed runtime tooling always warns (reported gaps).
Manifest coverage is limited to .csproj, package.json and central props; a top-level tests/ directory and a missing adjacent package-lock.json only warn.
An approval counts only as a dated Accepted-decisions row (or a linked docs/decisions record) naming the project or the 'From -> To' edge; direction or negation of approval is not parsed (reported).
Per-file manifest-checker arguments must resolve inside the active root; warnings alone yield success and missing selected files return no findings (reported uncertainty).
npm command versions must be exact three-component semver, while local paths, URLs, git sources and archives count as pinned (reported: immutability is not examined).
Recognized removals, versionless updates/audit-fix and peer-bypass options are blocked with no recorded-approval escape; the force check also covers pnpm/yarn and restore commands.
dotnet help is exempt; package commands accept two-to-four numeric version components; recognized removals always block; reference commands are classified regardless of consequence.
The command classifier inspects shell wrappers only when they carry recognized inline commands; script-file execution is not inspected before it runs (reported uncertainty).
Allowed references are inferred from project-name suffixes and fixed test-role tables; Api-to-Domain is allowed and unknown projects are unclassified (reported accuracy limits).
Named library families (@ngrx, axios, lodash, bootstrap, tailwind) and Angular build tooling in runtime dependencies always warn, with no suppression for a documented concrete need.
EF package checks target only recognized Domain/Application roles and seed/model/migration detection depends on exact Infrastructure/Persistence folder patterns (reported heuristics).
Any matching model-path change without a matching seeder or migration change triggers reminders, and any matching change suppresses them (reported relevance gaps).
xUnit, MSTest and TUnit in test projects or central versions always produce a warning, even when deliberately established (reported).
Active-root resolution prefers worktree/enclosing instruction roots, and the CLI can fall back to the script root when the cwd lacks .claude (reported uncertainty).
Checker text decoding rejects NUL-containing non-BOM input, and file walks skip named build/tool directories and nested Git roots.
The checker XML reader is a minimal textual parser requiring quoted attributes, not an evaluated MSBuild graph or a complete XML validator (reported uncertainty).
Hook execution is tied to the named tool events, node and the project-directory launcher, with a 30-second PreToolUse timeout and 60-second Post/Failure/Stop timeouts.
Actual-state enforcement uses a 5000-entry limit and selected manifest, input and instruction paths, excluding ignored directories and settings.local.json.
The actual-state checker persists a per-worktree snapshot, or a lowercased-root temporary-file snapshot outside Git, and re-baselines automatically on unreadable state (reported uncertainty).
Added or removed non-test projects and all reference-edge changes are errors unless recorded approval exists; only deltas still differing from HEAD are reported.
Actual-state attribution is limited by first-observation and moved-HEAD baselines; overflow reverts to dirty-file checks and there is no initial non-Git reference baseline (reported uncertainty).

The test reminder triggers for any non-deleted backend production .cs change without a backend test-path change, and any test-path change suppresses it (reported: may over-trigger or miss coverage needs).
Co-change hook reminders are deduplicated by triggering-path content with the latest 100 fingerprints; the CLI always reports and non-Git trees are skipped.

The instruction checker hard-codes the Kind/Scope vocabularies, four capability slots, required workflows and knowledge skills, banned standalone serilog/resilience skills, hook coverage and a 6000-token warning threshold.
Only CLAUDE.md may contain @ imports, it must import the decision register, and only OP/DEC artifacts may be imported.
Skills need matching directory/frontmatter names and descriptions; descriptions over 450 characters and reviewer bodies over 15 non-blank lines warn; template-maintenance must be user-only.
Backtick references must resolve without ambiguity; private references stay in their skill; dependency ranks and scope coverage are enforced, with routing, enforcement and dormant-pointer exceptions.
Enforcement files must declare every cited policy owner in a Conforms list on the line after the header and target only permitted STD/DEC owners.
Slot bindings need a stated role or reason; only leaves bind and only to the architecture frame; required leaf-to-frame bindings must be present.
Only the agreed slot directories and the selected module may exist; no unselected implementation stays in the tree and every capability artifact must be a listed facet of the selected module.
Module fields, name tokens, facet headers, fixed locations and contract-coverage rows must match; non-knowledge facet file names may not include implementation names.
A lexical leak check forbids naming the selected implementation outside its module, the map, the register selection block/decision log and project-owned files.
MAP.md must list every collected artifact, list no missing path and have a capability view per slot.
Hook settings must use exact node exec arguments, event matchers and 1-600 s timeouts; only four events are allowed and only PreToolUse may fail closed.
Conformance cycles fail; approximate token budgets only warn; the CLI exits nonzero only for errors.

FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate; validation at its owning boundary (Api transport, Application rules, Domain invariants, Infrastructure external assumptions); no mechanical duplication across layers (reported as additions).

Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context, are injected explicitly, and IUnitOfWork never becomes a repository container or service locator (reported: explicit injection beyond the constructor-injection default).

Liveness avoids external dependencies whose unavailability could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on required capabilities and must reflect startup and dependency availability (reported as 'must' rather than normally/should).
Substantial seed construction lives in a dedicated internal DbSeeder in Persistence/Seeding/, exposed through a narrow Infrastructure initialization extension (reported: exact directory prescribed).

Clear, correct code first; no specialized optimization without a concrete reason; measurement/profiling evidence for non-trivial optimizations (reported as part of the default rather than preferred evidence).
NUnit is the default .NET test framework; an established project deliberately using another framework follows it; no second framework without a concrete reason.

Typical test references: Domain.Tests to Domain; Application.Tests to Application (Domain as needed); IntegrationTests to Api (other layers through the host); Infrastructure.Tests to Infrastructure (reported: unclear whether 'typical' is enforceable).
Tests verify observable behavior and survive refactoring; interaction verification only when the interaction is the specified behavior (reported as strengthening 'normally survive').
Every NuGet or npm addition, update or removal runs the add-dependency workflow (reported: removals included).
Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS; in-app HTTP redirection is not required where the deployment provides the secure boundary and redirection is not desired.

npm is the frontend package manager unless deliberately changed; package.json and package-lock.json are committed and kept consistent; build/test tooling belongs in devDependencies unless there is a concrete reason.

Frontend structure stays feature-oriented: no application-wide technical buckets or empty architecture folders; feature code stays in its feature; core/shared stay small (reported as a prohibition rather than general avoidance).
The code-reviewer agent disallows Write, Edit and NotebookEdit (reported: other mutation tools such as the shell are not covered by the read-only policy).
The architecture slot requires exactly one frame implementation that defines the stable role vocabulary, with placement owned by the frame and technique by the leaves.
A frame implementation must provide the eleven listed contract items and exactly the fixed role-named facet locations, including a deterministic reference check.

The backend-testing slot is a required single implementation bound to the architecture frame; the neutral standard and the dotnet-testing skill name stay unchanged and a framework-consistency check is mandatory.
The optional frontend slot has zero or one implementation in frontend/<Name>.Web/ and its neutral standards stay unchanged on replacement.
Frontend facets use fixed role-named locations; selecting none removes those locations while pointers to them stay dormant.
The persistence slot requires ten contract items and fixed facet paths, including declared properties and deterministic enforcement.

EF Core types live only in Infrastructure; UnitOfWork implements IUnitOfWork over the shared scoped AppDbContext; persistence code sits in Infrastructure/Persistence/ (reported as binding layout details).
PreToolUse errors fail closed (block the command), while Post/Stop internal errors are visible non-blocking failures.
When the hook payload lacks cwd, dispatch falls back to process.cwd, so the repository checked may depend on the launcher environment (reported uncertainty).
Reference commands are blocked unless every discovered edge is recorded in an accepted decision (no-edge classifications stay blocked), and dependency guards block before execution.
Post-tool checks depend on a fixed shell/edit tool set and in-root path resolution; failed shell commands are inspected for changes too (reported uncertainty).
At Stop the co-change feedback blocks once per content state, skips a hook-triggered continuation and requires each reminder to be addressed or explained; outside a Git tree it is inactive.
The map assigns maintenance metadata owners, labels slot-contract changes Reserved and places optional detailed decision records in docs/decisions (reported as fixed bookkeeping).
Dependencies point WF to KNW to STD to DEC to OP and ENF to STD/DEC, declared on each ENF artifact's Conforms line; skill and agent references are routing pointers.
Product inputs never override policy.
Changes to the instruction system go through template-maintenance (user-invoked).

Changes to the instruction system go through the user-invoked template-maintenance workflow.
Changing a slot contract is a Reserved decision (rare).

Dependencies point WF to KNW to STD to DEC to OP and ENF to STD/DEC, declared on Conforms lines.
